entries.definition: Without delay, common in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 不耽搁，日常口语常用。

normalIntro.en: The hooks carry the missing middle from the adjective straight into the adverb ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把形容词里那个「缺席的中间」直接带进副词词尾。

normal.en: Take immediate and add -ly; the -ly says it answers the question when.
normal.cn: 在 immediate 后加 -ly：这个词尾说明它回答「何时」。

normal.en: Five beats, stress the second: im-ME-di-ate-ly.
normal.cn: 五个拍子，重音在第二：im-ME-di-ate-ly。

normal.en: Long words can still be urgent, and this one sits on every emergency sign.
normal.cn: 长词也能万分紧急，这个词就站在每个应急告示上。

normal.en: Pair it with after or before: immediately after the meeting, immediately before dawn.
normal.cn: 常与 after 或 before 搭配：会后立即、天亮前马上。

normal.en: Not immediately obvious is the polite way of saying very hard to see.
normal.cn: not immediately obvious 是「很难看出来」的客气说法。

abstract.en: The adverb measures a gap that is not there, and in doing so it refuses every excuse of delay.
abstract.cn: 这个副词所量的是并不存在的间隙，因此它拒绝一切拖延的借口。

abstract.en: In medicine the word saves lives, and in a queue it starts quarrels.
abstract.cn: 在急诊里这个词救人，在排队时它惹人争吵。

abstract.en: Immediately is the closest English comes to naming a moment that has no length.
abstract.cn: 在英语里，immediately 最接近命名一个没有长度的瞬间。

examples.en: Please reply immediately if you receive the notice.
examples.cn: 收到通知请立即回复。

examples.en: The stairs are immediately to your left.
examples.cn: 楼梯就在你左手边。

examples.en: It was not immediately clear why the flight was delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误的原因一时并不清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: immediate 立即的 + ly 副词尾——立即、马上；紧接地

root: immediate（拉丁语 in-「不」+ mediatus「居间」，即中间无隔）加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: no delay in time, direct connection in place or order, and emphatic instant response.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：时间上不拖延、地点或次序上直接相连，以及强调毫不迟疑的反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretcher wheeled straight down a corridor the moment the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，担架便被径直推进走廊。

branches.en: THE EMERGENCY LINE: call the doctor immediately is a life-saving instruction.
branches.cn: 急救线：「立刻叫医生」是救命的指令。

branches.en: THE MAP LINE: immediately next to marks a position with no gap.
branches.cn: 地图线：紧挨着表示不留空隙的位置。

branches.en: THE CONVERSATION LINE: immediately said no marks a decision without pause.
branches.cn: 对话线：一口回绝标记的是没有停顿的决定。

branches.en: THE GAP LINE: both senses come straight from the Latin word for middle.
branches.cn: 间隙线：两种用法都直接源自拉丁语的「中间」。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: signs and regulations use it to forbid waiting.
branches.cn: 告示线：告示与规章用它来禁止等待。

intro.en: Immediately is a Latin-derived adjective with a native adverb ending, a very common English hybrid.
intro.cn: immediately 是拉丁来源的形容词加本土副词词尾，是极常见的英式混搭。

latinIntro.en: The negative prefix and the middle root are Latin, while the -ly is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀与「中间」词根来自拉丁语，而 -ly 属日耳曼语。

items.example: Immortal shares it.
items.exampleCN: immortal 也用这一前缀。

items.example: Mediate carries the same root.
items.exampleCN: mediate 带同一词根。

items.example: An immediate decision was needed.
items.exampleCN: 需要一个立即的决定。

items.example: The lights went out immediately.
items.exampleCN: 灯立刻灭了。

items.meaning: in a certain way or at a certain time
items.meaningCN: 副词词尾，表方式或时间
items.example: Quickly and lately both use it.
items.exampleCN: quickly 与 lately 都用它。

items.example: The report has great immediacy.
items.exampleCN: 这篇报道很有现场感。

items.example: An intermediate step was needed.
items.exampleCN: 需要一个中间步骤。

items.meaning: one who stands in the middle
items.example: The mediator spoke last.
items.exampleCN: 调解人最后发言。

definition_en: extremely large in size, amount or degree
core_image: 站在山脚仰望那面占据整片天空的岩壁
scene: 火车穿过荒原开了六个小时，窗外仍是一片同一种草色。The plain looked immense, and the passengers stopped talking to watch it pass.
sceneCN: 这里 immense 是「巨大的、广大的」（第 1 个义项：面积或规模极大），句意是平原看上去无边无际，乘客们停下谈话望着它掠过。画面里有六小时不变的同色草原。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的、极大的、广大的

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: far larger than usual, hard to take in at one look
senses.definitionCN: 远大于寻常，一眼难以收进视野
senses.example: An immense cliff rose above the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一道巨大的崖壁耸立在港口上方。
senses.why: The Latin root means measured, and the prefix denies it: immense is what cannot be measured.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「度量」，前缀加以否定：immense 就是量不出来的东西。

senses.title: Very great in amount or degree
senses.definition: used of feelings, pressure or wealth on an extreme scale
senses.definitionCN: 形容感受、压力或财富达到极端程度
senses.example: The team worked under immense pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队承受着巨大的压力。
senses.why: Anything beyond measure can be weight or emotion as easily as rock, so the word moved from space to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 凡超出度量之物，既可以是岩石，也可以是压力或情绪，于是词义由空间移向感受。

senses.title: Very impressive or enjoyable
senses.definition: used informally in British speech to praise something warmly
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中热情称赞某物
senses.example: The concert last night was immense.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚的音乐会太棒了。
senses.why: Young speech reuses extreme-size words for praise, so an immense crowd becomes an immense evening.
senses.whyCN: 年轻人的口语常借表示「极大」的词来赞美，于是 immense crowd 变成 immense evening。

intro.en: Immense carries a Latin word for measuring, cancelled by a negative prefix: it names what has no measure.
intro.cn: immense 含一个拉丁语的「度量」词，被否定前缀抵消：它命名的是无法计量之物。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure, and mensus was its past participle, measured.
items.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，过去分词 mensus 即「量过的」。

items.en: Immansus or immensus described what was unmeasured and beyond reckoning.
items.cn: immanus 或 immensus 形容未加丈量、难以估算之物。

items.en: Poets used immensus of the sea, night and the heavens.
items.cn: 诗人用 immensus 形容大海、黑夜与天空。

items.en: French carried immense, and it kept the grand, slightly poetic air.
items.cn: 法语沿承 immense，仍带宏大而略富诗意的气韵。

items.en: English adopted it, later extending it to pressure, wealth and informal praise.
items.cn: 英语引入后，进一步扩展到压力、财富与口语赞美。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same measure root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for great size.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「度量」词根的词；近义组收其他表示庞大的词。

entries.definition: Very much, the adverb formed from this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 非常、极大地，由本词构成的副词。

entries.definition: The quality of being vast.
entries.definitionCN: 广大、浩瀚。

entries.definition: To find the size of something, the root that the prefix denies.
entries.definitionCN: 量出大小，正是前缀所否定的那个词根。

entries.definition: Very big, the most common word of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大，这组里最常用的词。

entries.definition: Extremely wide, used of areas and amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 极其辽阔，多用于面积与数量。

entries.definition: Beyond normal size, literally out of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 超出常规尺寸，字面是「出格」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rest on the measure root and the cancelled prefix, and on trains crossing endless plains.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子立在「度量」词根与被抵消的前缀上，也立在穿越荒原的火车上。

normal.en: Im- is not, mens is measure, so immense is unmeasurable.
normal.cn: im- 是不，mens 是度量，所以 immense 就是「量不出来」。

normal.en: The same mens sits inside measure and dimension.
normal.cn: 同一个 mens 也藏在 measure 与 dimension 里。

normal.en: Two syllables, stress the second: im-MENSE.
normal.cn: 两个音节，重音在后：im-MENSE。

normal.en: Immense pressure and immense wealth show the word is about scale, not only rock.
normal.cn: 巨大压力与巨额财富说明这个词讲的是尺度，不只是石头。

normal.en: Add -ly and immense becomes a strong very: immensely grateful.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 就变成加强版的 very：immensely grateful。

abstract.en: The word measures by refusing to measure, the same trick as calling a sea unending.
abstract.cn: 这个词用拒绝度量来表示度量之大，与称大海无边是同一种手法。

abstract.en: Anything immense forces the eye to move, so the word always implies a small viewer.
abstract.cn: 凡巨大之物都迫使眼睛转动，所以这个词总隐含着一个渺小的观看者。

abstract.en: Feelings borrow their size from space, which is why we call grief immense and not merely strong.
abstract.cn: 情感借空间的尺度来说大小，所以我们说悲伤巨大，而不只说悲伤强烈。

examples.en: The desert stretched out beneath them, immense and silent.
examples.cn: 沙漠在他们下方延展开来，宽广而寂静。

examples.en: She has brought immense energy to the project.
examples.cn: 她为这个项目投入了巨大的精力。

examples.en: We are immensely grateful for your help.
examples.cn: 我们对你的帮助极为感激。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + mens 度量 + e——量不出来的，即巨大无边的

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」（分词 mensus）加否定前缀 in- 成 immensus「无法丈量的」，经法语 immense 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: huge in space, extreme in amount, and immense in colloquial praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：空间上巨大、数量或程度上极端，以及口语中的「极好」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cliff wall taking up the entire sky above a small climber.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道占据整片天空的岩壁，崖下是渺小的攀登者。

branches.en: THE LANDSCAPE LINE: cliffs and plains defeat the eye.
branches.cn: 风景线：崖壁与原野让眼睛投降。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE LINE: emotions and workloads are called immense too.
branches.cn: 压力线：情绪与工作量也称 immense。

branches.en: THE SLANG LINE: young British speakers praise with it.
branches.cn: 俚语线：英国年轻人用它赞美。

branches.en: THE SCALE LINE: the word always answers how much, never how.
branches.cn: 尺度线：这个词永远回答「多大」，从不回答「怎样」。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: its two softer senses both concern attitude.
branches.cn: 感受线：两个较软的义项都与态度有关。

intro.en: Immense is a negative prefix on the Latin measure root, with -ly and -ity forms built on top.
intro.cn: immense 是否定前缀加拉丁语度量词根，上面再长出 -ly 与 -ity 形式。

latinIntro.en: Metiri and its participle mensus are standard Latin, and immensus is a common poetic word.
latinIntro.cn: metiri 及其分词 mensus 是标准拉丁成分，immensus 则是常见的诗语。

items.example: Impatient begins the same way.
items.exampleCN: impatient 也是同一前缀。

items.example: Dimension hides the same root.
items.exampleCN: dimension 藏着同一词根。

items.example: An immense wave broke over the boat.
items.exampleCN: 一个巨浪打在船上。

items.example: He was immensely proud.
items.exampleCN: 他极为自豪。

items.example: The immensity of the sky frightened her.
items.exampleCN: 天空的浩瀚令她害怕。

items.example: Measure the room before buying the rug.
items.exampleCN: 买地毯前先量一下房间。

items.example: It is only two dimensions on paper.
items.exampleCN: 在纸上它只有两个维度。

items.example: Pay should be commensurate with skill.
items.exampleCN: 报酬应与技能相称。

definition_en: a person who comes to live permanently in another country
core_image: 机场到达大厅里推着行李车、手里攥着旧护照的人
scene: 清晨的到达厅灯还没全亮，已经有几家人聚在出口旁边。Many immigrants arrived that week, and volunteers handed out water and city maps.
sceneCN: 这里 immigrant 是「移民」（第 1 个义项：移入另一国定居的人），句意是那一周许多移民抵达，志愿者分发水和城市地图。画面里有到达大厅、行李车和旧护照。

pos.zh: 名词：移民、外来移民

senses.title: A person who moves in to settle
senses.definition: someone who leaves one country to live permanently in another
senses.definitionCN: 离开一国、到另一国长期定居的人
senses.example: Her grandparents were immigrants from Ireland.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母是来自爱尔兰的移民。
senses.why: The prefix in- marks moving inward, so the word looks at the newcomer from the side of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 标示「向内移动」，因此这个词是从抵达地的视角看新来者。

senses.title: A member of a growing community
senses.definition: used collectively for groups whose labour and families reshape a city
senses.definitionCN: 集合使用，指以劳动与家庭改变一座城市的人群
senses.example: Immigrants opened most of the shops on that street.
senses.exampleCN: 那条街上的多数店铺都是移民开的。
senses.why: News and policy talk of immigrants in groups, so the singular noun often stands for a social category.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与政策常成组谈论移民，于是这个单数名词常代表一个社会类别。

senses.title: Frequently paired with a status word
senses.definition: used with words such as illegal or skilled to describe legal position or training
senses.definitionCN: 与 illegal、skilled 等词连用，说明法律身份或技能
senses.example: Skilled immigrants filled the vacant jobs quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 技术移民很快填补了空缺岗位。
senses.why: Because immigration is regulated, the word habitually takes a second word marking where a person stands in law.
senses.whyCN: 由于移入受管控，这个词习惯性地带一个说明法律身份的第二词。

intro.en: Immigrant is built from a Latin verb for moving into a place, and it was coined in English quite late.
intro.cn: immigrant 由拉丁语「迁入」动词构成，在英语里出现得相当晚。

items.en: Migrare meant to move from one place to another, whether a person or a bird.
items.cn: 拉丁语 migrare 意为从一处迁往另一处，人和鸟都可用。

items.en: Immigrare added the direction inward, the arrival into a new land.
items.cn: 加上表示向内的前缀后，immigrare 指迁入新的地方。

items.en: The participle immigrans named a person in the act of moving in.
items.cn: 分词 immigrans 指正在迁入的一个人。

items.en: English coined immigrant in the late eighteenth century, when migration was beginning to be counted and debated.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末造出 immigrant，当时人口迁徙刚开始被统计与争论。

items.en: The word spread through newspapers and census tables, always tilting towards the receiving country.
items.cn: 这个词通过报纸与人口普查表传播，始终倾向接收国的视角。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the migr- family; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who move.
note.cn: 形近组收 migr- 迁徙词根家族；近义组收表示迁移者的词。

entries.definition: One who leaves a country, the out- version of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国的人，是本词的「向外」版。

entries.definition: The process or policy side of the same movement.
entries.definitionCN: 同一迁徙过程或政策层面。

entries.definition: A mover without the in- prefix, often for work or season.
entries.definitionCN: 不带 in- 前缀的迁徙者，常指为工作或季节迁徙。

entries.definition: Anyone newly arrived, with no legal sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 新到的人，完全无法律含义。

entries.definition: One who takes land and stays, often in a colonial context.
entries.definitionCN: 占地定居者，多用于殖民语境。

entries.definition: One who flees danger, a distinct legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 逃离危险者，属一种独立的法定身份。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the in- and ex- pair, the migr- root, and the arrival hall image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用上 in- 与 ex- 的对立、migr- 词根，以及到达大厅的画面。

normal.en: Im-migr-ant: move in, versus e-migr-ant: move out.
normal.cn: im-migr-ant 是移入，e-migr-ant 是移出。

normal.en: The root migr- is the same one in migrate and migration, the act of moving.
normal.cn: 词根 migr- 也见于 migrate 与 migration，即迁移这一动作。

normal.en: Three beats, stress the first: IM-mi-grant.
normal.cn: 三个拍子，重音在前：IM-mi-grant。

normal.en: -ant marks a person, like servant and applicant.
normal.cn: -ant 标示人，如 servant 与 applicant。

normal.en: Immigrant and emigrant describe one traveller twice: leaving there, arriving here.
normal.cn: immigrant 与 emigrant 是同一个旅人的两面：从那边离开，到这边抵达。

abstract.en: The word depends on point of view: the same journey makes a person an emigrant on one coast and an immigrant on the other.
abstract.cn: 这个词取决于视角：同一趟旅程，在一岸是移出者，在另一岸是移入者。

abstract.en: Behind every statistic stands a bag with too few clothes and a name that others still struggle to say.
abstract.cn: 每个统计数字背后都站着一个行李装得太薄的人，和一个别人还念不准的名字。

abstract.en: A country measures immigration in numbers, but lives it in kitchens and classrooms.
abstract.cn: 国家用数字衡量移民，却在厨房与教室里经历它。

examples.en: The city grew quickly because immigrants kept arriving.
examples.cn: 移民不断到来，这座城市迅速扩张。

examples.en: Many immigrant families keep two languages at home.
examples.cn: 许多移民家庭在家里保留两种语言。

examples.en: He came to Britain as an immigrant in the 1970s.
examples.cn: 他在上世纪七十年代作为移民来到英国。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + migr 迁移 + ant 人——迁进来定居的人，即移民

root: 拉丁语 migrare「迁移」加向内前缀 in- 成 immigrare「迁入」，分词 immigrans，英语十八世纪末造 immigrant。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an individual settler, a social group, and a status-qualified category.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：移入定居的个人、作为社会群体的移民，以及带身份限定的类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a luggage trolley and an old passport in a half-lit arrivals hall.
core.cn: 核心意象：半亮的到达大厅里，行李车与一本旧护照。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: one family moving in and staying.
branches.cn: 个人线：一家人迁入并留下来。

branches.en: THE GROUP LINE: whole streets change shape with them.
branches.cn: 群体线：整条街的面貌因他们而变。

branches.en: THE STATUS LINE: skilled, illegal, recent qualify the word.
branches.cn: 身份线：skilled、illegal、recent 都在限定这个词。

branches.en: THE CENSUS LINE: governments count them for policy.
branches.cn: 普查线：政府为他们统计以定政策。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: immigrant often appears before families and workers.
branches.cn: 家庭线：这个词常出现在 families 与 workers 之前。

intro.en: Immigrant is a prefix, a Latin root and the person-marking -ant, with a full directional family.
intro.cn: immigrant 是前缀、拉丁词根与标示人的 -ant 的组合，周围有一套方向对立词。

latinIntro.en: Migrare and imm-igrare are attested in Latin, so the direction of the prefix is well founded.
latinIntro.cn: migrare 与 immigrare 在拉丁语中均有文献，前缀的方向有据可依。

items.example: Import uses the same inward prefix.
items.exampleCN: import 用同一个向内前缀。

items.meaning: to move from place to place
items.example: Birds migrate south each autumn.
items.exampleCN: 候鸟每年秋天向南迁徙。

items.example: Servant and assistant follow this pattern.
items.exampleCN: servant 与 assistant 都属此类。

items.example: An immigrant opened the bakery.
items.exampleCN: 一位移民开了那家面包店。

items.example: Immigrants rebuilt the old district.
items.exampleCN: 移民重建了老城区。

items.meaning: to move in as a settler
items.example: They immigrated in 1998.
items.exampleCN: 他们于1998年移居入境。

items.meaning: the process or policy of moving in
items.example: Immigration is a national debate here.
items.exampleCN: 移民事宜在这里是全国性议题。

items.example: Emigrants left by the same port.
items.exampleCN: 移居国外的人也从同一个港口离开。

definition_en: not following accepted standards of right and wrong behaviour
core_image: 办公室里有人把公家的东西悄悄塞进自己的背包
scene: 加班的晚上只剩他一个人，柜门开着。Taking the printer home felt immoral to everyone in the department, though nothing in the handbook forbade it.
sceneCN: 这里 immoral 是「不道德的」（第 1 个义项：违背公认是非标准），句意是部门里人人都觉得把打印机拿回家不道德，尽管手册上没有禁止。画面里有独自加班的人、开着的柜门和塞进背包的东西。

pos.zh: 形容词：不道德的、违背道德的

senses.title: Against accepted standards of right
senses.definition: contrary to the moral rules a community holds
senses.definitionCN: 违背一个群体所持的道德准则
senses.example: Cheating poor customers is simply immoral.
senses.exampleCN: 欺骗穷顾客简直就是不道德的。
senses.why: The prefix is a straightforward negative on the Latin word for custom, so the word means against the mores of a community.
senses.whyCN: 前缀是对拉丁语「习俗」一词的直白否定，因此这个词意为违背共同体的风气与准则。

senses.title: Wrong even if legal
senses.definition: used to judge conduct that the law permits but conscience rejects
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判法律容许而良心反对的行为
senses.example: It may be legal to sell the drug, but many find it immoral.
senses.exampleCN: 卖这种药也许合法，但很多人认为不正当。
senses.why: Because the word answers to custom rather than statute, it can condemn what courts allow.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词依据的是风气而非法条，它能谴责法院所容许的事。

senses.title: Used of gains and profits
senses.definition: describing money earned in a way that harms others
senses.definitionCN: 形容以损害他人方式赚来的钱
senses.example: They refused immoral profits from the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝从这门生意中获取不义之财。
senses.why: Gain is the commonest test case of morality, so the adjective attaches readily to profit and money.
senses.whyCN: 利益是道德最常见的试金石，于是这个形容词常与利润、钱财搭配。

intro.en: Immoral negatives a Latin word for custom and manners; oddly, the positive word moral is younger in English usage.
intro.cn: immoral 是对拉丁语「习俗、风气」一词的否定；有趣的是，肯定式 moral 在英语里出现得反而更晚。

items.en: Mos, plural mores, meant custom or manner, the unwritten habits of a people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mos（复数 mores）意为习俗、风气，即一个民族不成文的习惯。

items.en: Moralis was coined to describe what concerns such customs, and later what concerns right conduct.
items.cn: moralis 被用来形容与此类习俗相关之事，后来转为涉及正当行为。

items.en: French morale kept the sense of conduct and character.
items.cn: 法语 morale 保留行为与品格之意。

items.en: Immoral was used in English before moral settled, naming conduct against accepted custom.
items.cn: immoral 在 moral 定形之前就已在英语中使用，指违背公认习俗的行为。

items.en: Victorian debate sharpened the word, and it became a standard charge in law, church and press.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的争论使这个词更锋利，成了法律、教会与报纸的标准指控。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the moral family; the near-meaning group gathers other words of blame.
note.cn: 形近组收 moral 词族；近义组收其他表示指责的词。

entries.definition: Lacking moral sense altogether, rather than acting against it.
entries.definitionCN: 根本没有道德观念，而非有意违背。

entries.definition: Concerned with right behaviour; the base word.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及是非行为的，本词的原形。

entries.definition: The quality of being immoral, or an immoral act.
entries.definitionCN: 不道德的性质，或不道德的行为。

entries.definition: Against the rules of a profession or business, less about personal conscience.
entries.definitionCN: 违背行业规范，较少涉及个人良心。

entries.definition: Morally very bad, with a stronger emotional charge.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上极坏，情感色彩更重。

entries.definition: Willing to do wrong to get what one wants.
entries.definitionCN: 为达目的不惜行恶的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks separate immoral from amoral and tie the word to custom rather than law.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 immoral 与 amoral 分开，并把词义系在风气而非法律上。

normal.en: Im- is not, moral is right conduct: not right.
normal.cn: im- 是不，moral 是正当行为：也就是「不正当」。

normal.en: Immoral would mislead you, so keep a single m after the prefix: im-moral.
normal.cn: 别误写成 imm moral，前缀之后只有一个 m：im-moral。

normal.en: Three beats, stress the middle: im-MOR-al.
normal.cn: 三个拍子，重音在中间：im-MOR-al。

normal.en: Amoral removes the fault, immoral charges it; the prefix tells you which.
normal.cn: amoral 抽掉了过错，immoral 指控过错，换个前缀就换了态度。

normal.en: Moral came from mores, the customs people honour; the word judges against a community.
normal.cn: moral 源自 mores（人们遵守的习俗），这个词是拿共同体的标准来评判。

abstract.en: The word speaks in the voice of a community, so arguments about it rarely settle on facts alone.
abstract.cn: 这个词用共同体的声音说话，因此关于它的争论很少只靠事实了结。

abstract.en: Something legal can still be immoral, and that gap is where most of our hardest questions live.
abstract.cn: 合法之事仍可能不道德，我们最难的问题大多住在这道缝隙里。

abstract.en: Immoral names a broken custom, not a broken law, so the accused may never see a judge.
abstract.cn: immoral 命名的是被破坏的风俗，而非被违反的法条，被告也许永远见不到法官。

examples.en: Many workers thought the pay cut was immoral.
examples.cn: 许多工人认为降薪不道德。

examples.en: He was condemned for immoral conduct in office.
examples.cn: 他因任职期间不道德的行为而受到谴责。

examples.en: There is nothing immoral about asking for help.
examples.cn: 寻求帮助没有任何不道德之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + moral 道德的——不道德的；注意与 amoral（无道德意识的）分开

root: 拉丁语 mos（复数 mores）「习俗、风气」→ moralis「与习俗相关的」，加否定前缀 in-（在 m 前作 im-）构成 immoral。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: against community custom, wrong though legal, and used of gains.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：违背群体习俗、合法但不正当，以及用于钱财的「不义」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: office goods slipped quietly into a private bag at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里把公家物件悄悄塞进私人背包。

branches.en: THE NEIGHBOUR LINE: the community's standards do the judging.
branches.cn: 邻里线：由共同体的标准来评判。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: the word can stand outside the statute book.
branches.cn: 法律线：这个词可以站在法典之外。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: tainted profits are its favourite target.
branches.cn: 金钱线：不义之财是它最常针对的对象。

branches.en: THE CONSCIENCE LINE: both senses appeal to an inner court.
branches.cn: 良心线：两种用法都诉诸一个内心的法庭。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST LINE: moral and amoral sit on either side as counterwords.
branches.cn: 对照线：moral 与 amoral 分立两侧，构成反衬。

intro.en: Immoral is the negative of a Latin custom word, with a small family that includes its mild look-alike amoral.
intro.cn: immoral 是拉丁语「习俗」词的否定形，同族中还有容易混淆的 amoral。

latinIntro.en: Mos, mores and moralis are recorded in Latin; the prefix im- is in- assimilated before m.
latinIntro.cn: mos、mores 与 moralis 均有拉丁文献；前缀 im- 是 in- 在 m 前的同化形式。

items.example: Impossible uses the same negative.
items.exampleCN: impossible 用同一否定前缀。

items.example: Mores is the same root as a Latin plural.
items.exampleCN: mores 正是该词根的拉丁复数形式。

items.example: Natural and legal use it too.
items.exampleCN: natural 与 legal 也用。

items.example: The deal was widely called immoral.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易被普遍称为不道德。

items.meaningCN: 一般不用比较级，作绝对判断
items.example: Most people called it simply immoral.
items.exampleCN: 多数人只说它不道德。

items.meaning: the state or an act of being immoral
items.example: The paper attacked official immorality.
items.exampleCN: 该报抨击官员的不道德行为。

items.example: They acted immorally but legally.
items.exampleCN: 他们行事不道德却合法。

items.example: A machine is amoral, not immoral.
items.exampleCN: 机器无所谓不道德，它没有道德意识。

definition_en: a strong effect on someone or something, or the force of one object hitting another
core_image: 石子落进水塘，圈纹一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 新地铁线开通三个月后，站边小店换了两轮老板。The impact on the neighbourhood was clear from the empty shops and the new coffee queue.
sceneCN: 这里 impact 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对人或事产生的强烈作用），句意是对这一带的影响从空掉的店铺和新排起的咖啡队就能看出。画面里有地铁口的波纹状人潮。

pos.zh: 名词：影响、冲击；撞击
动词：影响、冲击；撞击

senses.title: A strong effect
senses.definition: a powerful effect that something has on a situation or person
senses.definitionCN: 某物对局势或人产生的强烈作用
senses.example: The new policy had an impact on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策对小店产生了影响。
senses.why: The word began as physical striking and was carried over to anything that strikes a situation the way a stone strikes water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指实物的撞击，后来扩展到一切像石子击水般击中局面的东西。

senses.title: The force of a collision
senses.definition: the moment and force of one body striking another
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体击中另一物体的即刻与力度
senses.example: The windscreen cracked on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 挡风玻璃一撞就裂了。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, kept in physics and in accident reports.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，保留在物理学与事故报道里。

senses.title: To affect or to hit
senses.definition: to have an effect on something, or to strike it forcefully
senses.definitionCN: 对某物产生影响，或用力撞上
senses.example: Rising costs impact every household.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上涨冲击着每一个家庭。
senses.why: English turns almost any strong noun into a verb, and impact took that route in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 英语几乎能把任何强势名词变动词，impact 在二十世纪就走上了这条路。

intro.en: Impact began as a Latin participle meaning driven in or pressed against, and only later became a noun for effect.
intro.cn: impact 最初是拉丁语分词，意为「打入、压向」，后来才成为表示「影响」的名词。

items.en: Pangere meant to fasten or strike, and its participle pactus described something fixed or driven in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pangere 意为固定或击打，其分词 pactus 描述被钉入或压紧之物。

items.en: Impactus was the strengthened form, pressed hard against something.
items.cn: impactus 是加强形式，意为被重重压向某物。

items.en: English took impact in the seventeenth century as a term in mechanics for collision.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪以力学用语的「碰撞」义引入 impact。

items.en: In the twentieth century it broadened into the general sense of a strong effect.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，它扩展为泛指强烈影响。

items.en: Verb use grew after the 1950s and is now common in business writing.
items.cn: 动词用法在1950年代后增多，如今在商务写作中很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same pacting root; the near-meaning group gathers words for effect.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「钉入、击打」词根的词；近义组收表示作用的词。

entries.definition: An agreement fixed between parties, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 各方订立的约定，同根。

entries.definition: Pressed closely together, sharing the fastening root.
entries.definitionCN: 紧压在一起的，同出「紧固」之根。

entries.definition: The state of being wedged or pressed in, especially in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 被卡住压紧的状态，多用于医学。

entries.definition: A result caused by something; quieter than impact.
entries.definitionCN: 由某物引起的结果，语气比 impact 平。

entries.definition: The power to change how someone acts or thinks.
entries.definitionCN: 改变他人行为或想法的力量。

entries.definition: The physical crashing of two objects, close to sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 两个物体的实体相撞，接近第二个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the Latin fastening root to ripples on a pond and to business verb use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁「钉紧」词根连到水塘涟漪与商务动词用法上。

normal.en: The root pact means fixed together, as in a peace pact; impact is a blow that fixes a mark.
normal.cn: 词根 pact 意为固定在一起，如和平协定；impact 是留下痕迹的击打。

normal.en: Noun stress first: IM-pact; verb often the same in modern English.
normal.cn: 名词重音在前：IM-pact；现代英语动词常同音。

normal.en: Have an impact on is the safest phrase: preposition on, not for.
normal.cn: 最稳的搭配是 have an impact on，介词用 on。

normal.en: On impact is the expression in crash reports.
normal.cn: 事故报道里用 on impact 表示「撞击时」。

normal.en: A stone, a policy and a rumour can all make the same ripples.
normal.cn: 石子、政策与谣言都能激起同样的涟漪。

abstract.en: The word began with bodies meeting and ended with lives meeting, and the physics stayed.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于物体相遇，终于人生相遇，而那点物理学一直留着。

abstract.en: Impact measures what something leaves behind, so every use implies a before and an after.
abstract.cn: impact 衡量某物留下了什么，因此每次使用都隐含一个之前与一个之后。

abstract.en: A policy with no impact has failed quietly, and a person with impact has changed the room on entering.
abstract.cn: 毫无影响的政策是悄悄失败了，而有影响力的人一进屋就改变了房间。

examples.en: The report examines the impact of tourism on the coast.
examples.cn: 这份报告考察旅游业对海岸的影响。

examples.en: The car hit the barrier and the driver was thrown forward on impact.
examples.cn: 汽车撞上护栏，撞击时司机被向前抛出。

examples.en: Rising fuel prices impacted the whole industry.
examples.cn: 燃料涨价冲击了整个行业。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + pact 压紧（如 pact 协定）——狠狠压进去，即撞击；引申为冲击、影响

root: 拉丁语 pangere「钉入、击打」→ 分词 impactus「被压向的」，十七世纪进入英语作力学用语，二十世纪扩展为「影响」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a strong effect, a physical collision, and the verb made from both.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：强烈影响、实体撞击，以及由两者转来的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples from a dropped stone reaching the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：石子落水后，涟漪一直推到岸边。

branches.en: THE POLICY LINE: the word asks what changed after the decision.
branches.cn: 政策线：这个词问的是决定之后改变了什么。

branches.en: THE ACCIDENT LINE: on impact reports the instant of collision.
branches.cn: 事故线：on impact 报告相撞的一瞬。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS LINE: impact as a verb suits reports and meetings.
branches.cn: 商务线：impact 作动词适合理报告与开会。

branches.en: THE FORCE LINE: both senses carry a sense of something arriving hard.
branches.cn: 力量线：两种用法都带着「重重抵达」之感。

branches.en: THE RIPPLE LINE: the noun and verb name cause and consequence.
branches.cn: 涟漪线：名词与动词分别命名起因与后果。

intro.en: Impact is a Latin participle used as a noun, with a small modern family including a back-formed verb.
intro.cn: impact 是当作名词用的拉丁分词，现代又反向造出动词，形成一个小家族。

latinIntro.en: Pangere and impactus are recorded in Latin, and pact- supplies the fixed-agreement branch of the family.
latinIntro.cn: pangere 与 impactus 均有拉丁文献，pact- 这一支则长出「订约」的意义。

items.example: Import carries a similar inward sense.
items.exampleCN: import 也有类似的向内感。

items.example: The root also gives pact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也造出 pact。

items.example: The impact was felt for years.
items.exampleCN: 其影响持续多年。

items.example: Drought impacts food prices.
items.exampleCN: 干旱冲击粮价。

items.example: The area was badly impacted by the flood.
items.exampleCN: 这一带受洪水影响严重。

items.example: Noise is impacting residents.
items.exampleCN: 噪音正影响居民。

items.example: They wanted an impactful opening.
items.exampleCN: 他们想要一个有力的开场。

items.example: The two sides signed a pact.
items.exampleCN: 双方签署了一项协定。

definition_zh: 不耐烦的；急躁的；急切的
definition_en: annoyed by waiting, or wanting something to happen very soon
core_image: 排队时不停看表、把重心从一只脚换到另一只脚的人
scene: 银行只开了一个窗口，队尾那位每隔十秒就看一眼手机。He grew impatient before the clerk had even called the first number.
sceneCN: 这里 impatient 是「不耐烦的」（第 1 个义项：因等待而恼火），句意是柜员还没叫第一个号，他就已经不耐烦了。画面里有只开一个窗口的银行和不停看表的人。

pos.zh: 形容词：不耐烦的、急躁的；急切的

senses.title: Annoyed by delay
senses.definition: irritated because something takes longer than you want
senses.definitionCN: 因某事耗时过久而感到恼火
senses.example: The driver became impatient at the third red light.
senses.exampleCN: 第三个红灯时司机已经不耐烦了。
senses.why: Patient here means enduring, and the negative prefix says the endurance has run out.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 patient 意为「能忍受的」，否定前缀说明忍耐已经耗尽。

senses.title: Eager for something to happen
senses.definition: very keen and unable to wait calmly for a result
senses.definitionCN: 非常渴望结果而无法平静等待
senses.example: She was impatient for the exam results.
senses.exampleCN: 她急切地等着考试成绩。
senses.why: Losing the will to wait can point forward as well as backward, so the word also names hopeful eagerness.
senses.whyCN: 失去等待的耐性既可指向过去也可指向未来，于是这个词也指带着期待的急切。

senses.title: Short and sharp in manner
senses.definition: describing a movement or tone that shows irritation
senses.definitionCN: 形容流露出恼意的手势或语气
senses.example: He answered with an impatient wave of the hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他不耐烦地摆了摆手作答。
senses.why: Inward irritation soon shows as outward gesture, and English lets the adjective describe the gesture itself.
senses.whyCN: 内心的恼火很快外化为手势，英语允许这个形容词直接描述手势。

intro.en: Impatient negates the Latin word for suffering, for patience was the ability to bear things.
intro.cn: impatient 是对拉丁语「忍受」一词的否定，因为 patience 本指承受之力。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer or to undergo, and patiens described one who endured.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pati 意为忍受、经受，patiens 形容能够承受的人。

items.en: Impatiens added the negative: unable to bear, easily provoked by waiting.
items.cn: 加否定前缀成 impatiens：无法承受，容易被等待激怒。

items.en: The plant we call impatient got the name for bursting its seed pods at a touch.
items.cn: 我们称作凤仙花的那种植物，因蒴果一碰就炸而得名。

items.en: French used impacient, and the form passed into English writing.
items.cn: 法语作 impacient，这一形式进入英语书写。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as impatient and kept both the waiting sense and the eager sense.
items.cn: 英语把拼写定为 impatient，兼收「等不下去」与「急切盼望」两种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the patient family; the near-meaning group gathers words for irritation and hurry.
note.cn: 形近组收 patient 词族；近义组收表示烦躁与急促的词。

entries.definition: The state of being impatient.
entries.definitionCN: 不耐烦的状态。

entries.definition: In an impatient manner.
entries.definitionCN: 不耐烦地。

entries.definition: Able to wait calmly, the positive base word.
entries.definitionCN: 能够平静等待的，肯定形式。

entries.definition: Unable to stay still, often from boredom.
entries.definitionCN: 坐立不安，多因无聊。

entries.definition: Mildly angry, without the specific cause of waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 轻度恼怒，未必因等待。

entries.definition: Very keen to act; only the positive side of sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 非常想行动，只取第二个义项中积极的一面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks turn on the negative prefix and the hidden word for suffering inside patient.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子全靠否定前缀以及 patient 里藏着的「忍受」之意。

normal.en: Im- is not: impatient is not patient, and patient is the one who can suffer and wait.
normal.cn: im- 是不：impatient 就是不 patient，而 patient 本指能忍受、能等待的人。

normal.en: Im-patient, one m only: the prefix folds into the p that follows.
normal.cn: im-patient，只有一个 m：前缀并进了后面的 p。

normal.en: Three beats, stress the middle: im-PA-tient.
normal.cn: 三个拍子，重音在中间：im-PA-tient。

normal.en: The ending sounds like shent, the same soft sh that patient also carries.
normal.cn: 词尾读作 shent，与 patient 所带的那个柔和的 sh 相同。

normal.en: Impatient with people, impatient for news: two prepositions, two feelings.
normal.cn: impatient with 人，impatient for 消息：两个介词，两种心情。

abstract.en: The word quietly remembers that patience is a form of suffering bravely borne.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄记着：耐心原是一种被勇敢承受的痛苦。

abstract.en: Losing patience is losing the ability to let time pass, and clocks then seem to slow on purpose.
abstract.cn: 失去耐心就是失去让时间流过的能力，此后钟表仿佛故意变慢。

abstract.en: The same word covers impatience at a queue and eagerness for good news, since both refuse delay.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指排队时的烦躁，也指急盼好消息，因为两者都拒绝等待。

examples.en: Don't be so impatient; the train will come.
examples.cn: 别这么急躁，火车会来的。

examples.en: She was impatient to see her son again.
examples.cn: 她急切地想再见到儿子。

examples.en: The teacher was growing impatient with the same excuses.
examples.cn: 老师听到同样的借口渐渐不耐烦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + patient 能忍耐的——不能忍，即不耐烦的

root: 拉丁语 pati「忍受」→ patiens「能承受的」，加否定前缀 in-（在 p 前作 im-）成 impatiens，经法语 impacient 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: irritated by waiting, eager for what is coming, and showing that irritation in manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：因等待而恼、急切盼望将来的事，以及在举止上流露恼意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person shifting weight from foot to foot in a slow queue.
core.cn: 核心意象：慢队里不断换脚站着的人。

branches.en: THE QUEUE LINE: red lights and slow windows provoke it.
branches.cn: 排队线：红灯与慢窗口招来它。

branches.en: THE WAITING LINE: impatient for results is hopeful, not angry.
branches.cn: 等待线：急盼结果时是期盼而非恼怒。

branches.en: THE GESTURE LINE: a wave of the hand completes the meaning.
branches.cn: 手势线：一摆手就把意思说完了。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: the root cause is always delay.
branches.cn: 时间线：根本原因始终是拖延。

branches.en: THE FACE LINE: what begins inside shows on the face.
branches.cn: 面孔线：起于内心的东西会写在脸上。

intro.en: Impatient is a negative prefix on a Latin endurance word, with a full set of related forms.
intro.cn: impatient 是拉丁语「忍耐」词的否定形，配有整套相关形式。

latinIntro.en: Pati and patiens are standard Latin, and impatiens is attested in classical texts.
latinIntro.cn: pati 与 patiens 是标准拉丁成分，impatiens 在古典文献中可见。

items.example: Immoral uses the same negative.
items.exampleCN: immoral 也用它。

items.example: Patient and passion share it.
items.exampleCN: patient 与 passion 共用此根。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，表具备某性质
items.example: Obedient and ancient follow the pattern.
items.exampleCN: obedient 与 ancient 属同类。

items.meaning: usually used of a lasting state
items.meaningCN: 一般作状态形容，少用比较级
items.example: The whole queue was impatient by noon.
items.exampleCN: 到中午整条队都不耐烦了。

items.example: Her impatience showed in her voice.
items.exampleCN: 她的急躁从声音里透出来。

items.example: He tapped impatiently on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 他不耐烦地敲桌子。

items.example: Be patient for a moment.
items.exampleCN: 稍等片刻，耐心一点。

items.meaning: able to suffer together, hence fitting together
items.example: The two systems are compatible.
items.exampleCN: 这两个系统相互兼容。

definition_zh: 实施；执行；贯彻；（名词）工具、器具
definition_en: to put a plan or decision into effect, or a tool used for a particular job
core_image: 钉在车间墙上的新流程图，旁边挂着一把扳手
scene: 新规定贴在门口，第二周真的开始执行了。Once the manager decided to implement the safety rules, every worker had to sign the sheet before entering.
sceneCN: 这里 implement 是「实施、执行」（第 1 个义项：把计划变为实际做法），句意是经理一旦决定实施安全规定，每个工人进门前都要在表上签到。画面里有门口贴的新规定和墙上的流程图。

pos.zh: 动词：实施、执行、贯彻
名词：工具、器具、器械

derivatives.zh: （形近）作为工具或手段的、辅助实施的

senses.title: To carry a plan into effect
senses.definition: to take a decision, rule or plan and make it work in practice
senses.definitionCN: 把决定、规定或计划真正落实为做法
senses.example: The school will implement the new timetable in March.
senses.exampleCN: 学校将在三月实施新的课表。
senses.why: The Latin root means to fill up, and carrying out a plan fills the gap between intention and fact.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「填满」，而落实计划正是把「打算」与「事实」之间的空隙填满。

senses.title: A tool for a task
senses.definition: an object used to carry out a particular kind of work
senses.definitionCN: 用于完成某类工作的物件
senses.example: Old farm implements hang in the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓里挂着旧农具。
senses.why: A tool is what supplies a job with what it needs, so the filling root named the thing that fills the lack.
senses.whyCN: 工具正是为工作补上所缺之物，因此那个表示「填满」的词根也命名了补缺的物件。

senses.title: To put into practice as a duty
senses.definition: used of officials whose job is to make rules real
senses.definitionCN: 用于负责把规则落到实处的人员
senses.example: Inspectors must implement the standards without favour.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员必须不偏不倚地贯彻这些标准。
senses.why: When an institution delegates execution, the verb takes an official subject and gains a tone of duty.
senses.whyCN: 当机构把执行权委派下去时，这个动词的主语多为官方人员，语气带上职责感。

intro.en: Implement is built on a Latin verb meaning to fill up, and both tool and execution grow from that idea of supplying what is missing.
intro.cn: implement 建立在拉丁语「填满」动词之上，工具与执行两种用法都从「补上所缺」这一想法长出。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and its root sits inside plenus, full.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plere 意为填满，其词根也藏在 plenus（满的）之中。

items.en: Implere meant to fill up completely, to complete what was lacking.
items.cn: implere 意为彻底填满，把所缺的部分补齐。

items.en: Its participle impletum, with the noun implementum, named a filling and later a thing that fills a need.
items.cn: 其分词 impletum 与名词 implementum 指充填，后指满足需要的物件。

items.en: English took implement as a noun for equipment in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语以名词形式引入 implement，指装备器具。

items.en: The verb came much later, and in the twentieth century business and government made implement a standard word for carrying out policy.
items.cn: 动词用法出现得晚得多，二十世纪企业与政府把 implement 变成「执行政策」的标准词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the filling root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of carrying out.
note.cn: 形近组收「填满」词根的词；近义组收表示执行的动词。

entries.definition: The act of putting a plan into practice.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划付诸实行的行为。

entries.definition: Something that completes another, from the same filling root.
entries.definitionCN: 补足另一物之物，同出「填满」之根。

entries.definition: Fully filled, with nothing missing.
entries.definitionCN: 完全填满、一无所缺的。

entries.definition: To do what was planned, in plain everyday words.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划好的事做出来，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To perform a plan or order, often with legal or military weight.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计划或命令，常带法律或军事语气。

entries.definition: To put a rule or method to practical use.
entries.definitionCN: 把规则或方法用到实际中。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the filling root to a wrench on the wall and to a policy that must reach the shop floor.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「填满」词根连到墙上的扳手和必须落到车间的政策上。

normal.en: Im- in, ple- fill: implement is to fill the plan in with action.
normal.cn: im- 向内，ple- 填满：implement 就是把行动填进计划里。

normal.en: The verb stresses the first syllable in British English: IM-ple-ment.
normal.cn: 英式英语里动词重音在前：IM-ple-ment。

normal.en: Noun and verb share a spelling, unlike complement with an e.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，注意别与带 e 的 complement 混淆。

normal.en: A tool is what fills your hand with what the job needs.
normal.cn: 工具就是把干活所需之物填进你手里的东西。

normal.en: Policies are written in offices but implemented in shops and schools.
normal.cn: 政策写在办公室里，却是实施在店铺与学校里。

abstract.en: The word names the hardest half of any reform, the part after the announcement.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名的是一切改革中最难的那一半，即宣布之后的部分。

abstract.en: Its two senses meet in one idea: something missing gets supplied, by a hand tool or by a bureaucrat.
abstract.cn: 两个义项在一个想法里相遇：缺什么补什么，或用手里的工具，或用公职人员。

abstract.en: A good plan unimplemented is only a hope written down.
abstract.cn: 未能落地的良策，只是写下来的愿望。

examples.en: The government promised to implement the report's advice.
examples.cn: 政府承诺落实报告中的建议。

examples.en: Implementing the change took three months of training.
examples.cn: 实施这项变动花了三个月培训。

examples.en: Simple stone implements were found in the cave.
examples.cn: 洞中发现了简单的石制器具。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 使 + ple 填满 + ment 名词/动词尾——把空缺填满：实施；能补上所需之物的工具

root: 拉丁语 implere「填满」→ 分词 impletum、名词 implementum，十五世纪进入英语作名词「器具」，二十世纪衍生动词「实施」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: carrying out a plan, the tool used for work, and the official duty of making rules real.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：落实计划、干活用的工具，以及把规定真正落地的职务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a policy poster on a factory door beside a wrench hanging on a nail.
core.cn: 核心意象：车间门口的政策告示，旁边的钉子上挂着一把扳手。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: timetables and rules turn into actions.
branches.cn: 办公室线：课表与规定变成实际行动。

branches.en: THE BARN LINE: implements hang where farm work happens.
branches.cn: 谷仓线：农具挂在真正做农活的地方。

branches.en: THE DUTY LINE: inspectors implement standards without favour.
branches.cn: 职责线：检查员不偏不倚地贯彻标准。

branches.en: THE HANDS LINE: tools fill the hands, plans fill the calendar.
branches.cn: 手边线：工具填满双手，计划填满日程。

branches.en: THE FOLLOW-UP LINE: both name the work that comes after the decision.
branches.cn: 后续线：两者指的都是决定之后的活儿。

intro.en: Implement is a Latin filling verb turned English noun and then verb again, with a family of completion words.
intro.cn: implement 是拉丁语「填满」动词先变英语名词、再变动词，身边是一族「完备」词。

latinIntro.en: Plere and implere are recorded in Latin, and the participle supplies the English stem.
latinIntro.cn: plere 与 implere 均有拉丁文献，其分词提供了英语词干。

items.example: Import uses the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: import 用同一前缀。

items.example: The root also gives complete.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还造出 complete。

items.meaningCN: 表示物或结果的名词词尾
items.example: Equipment follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: equipment 同属此类。

items.meaning: a tool; to put into effect
items.example: They implemented the plan at once.
items.exampleCN: 他们立刻执行了计划。

items.example: The scheme was implemented last year.
items.exampleCN: 该方案去年已实施。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a plan
items.example: Implementation begins in January.
items.exampleCN: 实施从一月开始。

items.example: The set is complete.
items.exampleCN: 这套东西齐了。

items.meaning: something added to fill a lack
items.example: She takes an iron supplement.
items.exampleCN: 她在服用补铁剂。

latinEntries.meaning: a filling, a means of filling

definition_en: a meaning suggested but not stated, or a likely result that follows from something
core_image: 一句话说完后，听者脸上瞬间的迟疑
scene: 会上经理说预算「不会更少」，没人笑。The implication was that someone would be let go, though nobody had said so.
sceneCN: 这里 implication 是「暗示、言外之意」（第 1 个义项：未明说而蕴含的意思），句意是言外之意是有人要走，尽管没人说出来。画面里有迟疑的听者和会议室。

pos.zh: 名词：含义、暗示、言外之意；影响、后果；牵连

senses.title: A meaning not stated
senses.definition: an idea that the speaker or writer suggests without saying it directly
senses.definitionCN: 说者或作者未明说却暗示的意思
senses.example: The implication of his remark was clear to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句话的言外之意人人都懂。
senses.why: The Latin root means folded in, and a hinted meaning is folded inside the words rather than laid out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「折进里面」，被暗示的意思正是折在话语之内，而未摊开。

senses.title: A likely result
senses.definition: a consequence that a decision or fact is likely to bring
senses.definitionCN: 某项决定或事实很可能带来的后果
senses.example: The finding has implications for food safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现对食品安全有影响。
senses.why: A consequence is also folded inside a cause, waiting to unfold, so the same noun covers results.
senses.whyCN: 后果同样折在原因之内、等着被展开，于是同一个名词也涵盖结果。

senses.title: Involvement in wrongdoing
senses.definition: the fact of being involved in a crime or a scandal
senses.definitionCN: 卷入罪行或丑闻的事实
senses.example: His implication in the fraud ended his career.
senses.exampleCN: 他牵连进这起诈骗案，就此断送了事业。
senses.why: To be folded into an affair is exactly what involvement means, so the noun also reports guilt by association.
senses.whyCN: 被折进一桩事件，正是「牵连」，因此这个名词也用来报告「因关联而有嫌疑」。

intro.en: Implication is the Latin noun of folding in, and that physical image survives in every modern sense.
intro.cn: implication 是拉丁语的「折入」名词，这个具体意象在每种现代用法中都还活着。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and the fold could be cloth, a letter or an argument.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，可折的是布、信，也可是一套论证。

items.en: Implicare folded something into something else, and hence entangled it.
items.cn: implicare 指把一物折进另一物，因而也指卷入、缠上。

items.en: Implicatio named that entanglement or the act of folding in.
items.cn: implicatio 命名这种缠绕，或折入的动作。

items.en: French used implication for involvement and for meaning carried within words.
items.cn: 法语用 implication 表示卷入，也指话语内含的意思。

items.en: Logic gave English the sense of what follows from a statement, now the commonest use.
items.cn: 逻辑学赋予英语「由陈述推出什么」这一义，如今是最常见的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fold family; the near-meaning group gathers words for hinted meaning and consequence.
note.cn: 形近组收「折叠」词族；近义组收表示暗示与后果的词。

entries.definition: To suggest without stating, the verb behind this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 不说明而暗示，本名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Folded in, not openly expressed.
entries.definitionCN: 折在其中的、不显明表达的。

entries.definition: A difficulty folded together with the main matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与主要事情绞在一起的麻烦。

entries.definition: A result that follows, closer to sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 随之而来的结果，接近第二个义项。

entries.definition: A hint or idea put forward softly.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻提出的暗示或想法。

entries.definition: Being mixed up in an affair, close to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 卷入某事件，接近第三个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the folding image, which explains hidden meaning, hidden results and hidden guilt.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用「折」这个意象，它同时解释了隐义、隐果与隐罪。

normal.en: Plic means fold, so implication is what is folded inside a sentence.
normal.cn: plic 意为折，implication 就是折进句子里的东西。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: im-pli-CA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第三音节：im-pli-CA-tion。

normal.en: The verb is imply, the adjective implicit: all three wear the same fold.
normal.cn: 动词是 imply，形容词是 implicit，三者都带着同一个「折」。

normal.en: By implication is a useful phrase for reading between the lines.
normal.cn: by implication 是「读出弦外之音」的好用短语。

normal.en: Have implications for keeps the preposition for, not on.
normal.cn: have implications for 的介词是 for，不是 on。

abstract.en: A fold hides a surface and preserves it at once, which is why the word can mean both a secret meaning and a stored result.
abstract.cn: 折叠既藏起一面又保存它，所以这个词既能指隐藏的意思，也能指被存下的结果。

abstract.en: What is implied is present and absent at the same time, like an object under a cloth.
abstract.cn: 被暗示之物既在场又不在场，像布下的一件东西。

abstract.en: Arguments often move by implication, and the honest reader keeps unfolding the cloth.
abstract.cn: 论证常靠暗示推进，诚实的读者会不断把布展开。

examples.en: He objected to the implication that he had been careless.
examples.cn: 他反对那种暗示他不小心的说法。

examples.en: The new law has implications for every landlord.
examples.cn: 新法律对每个房东都有影响。

examples.en: She denied any implication in the scheme.
examples.cn: 她否认与这个计划有任何牵连。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + plic 折 + ation 名词——折进话里的意思：言外之意；折进事里的结果：影响

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折叠」→ implicare「折入、卷入」→ implicatio，经古法语 implication 进入英语，逻辑学使其定指「蕴含之义」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a hinted meaning, a likely consequence, and involvement in a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：暗示的意思、可能的后果，以及被卷进某桩事情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pause on the listeners' faces after a sentence ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：话说完后，听者脸上那一瞬的停顿。

branches.en: THE MEETING LINE: the implication is that signals bad news.
branches.cn: 会议线：the implication is that 常引出坏消息。

branches.en: THE POLICY LINE: implications for whole industries.
branches.cn: 政策线：对整行业的影响。

branches.en: THE COURT LINE: implication in a fraud ends careers.
branches.cn: 法庭线：牵连进诈骗会断送前程。

branches.en: THE FOLD LINE: a hint and a result are both folded inside something.
branches.cn: 折叠线：暗示与结果都折在某物之内。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE LINE: both senses report what follows from an act.
branches.cn: 后果线：两种用法都报告某种行为之后跟着来的东西。

intro.en: Implication is a Latin fold plus the noun ending -ation, in a family that includes imply and implicit.
intro.cn: implication 是拉丁语「折」加名词词尾 -ation，同族有 imply 与 implicit。

latinIntro.en: Plicare, implicare and implicatio are all recorded in Latin, so the folding image is documented.
latinIntro.cn: plicare、implicare 与 implicatio 在拉丁语中均有文献，「折」的意象有据。

items.example: Import shares the prefix.
items.exampleCN: import 同用此前缀。

items.example: The root also appears in complicate.
items.exampleCN: 该词根也见于 complicate。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: Explanation follows the pattern.
items.exampleCN: explanation 同属此类。

items.example: The implication was unmistakable.
items.exampleCN: 言外之意再明显不过。

items.example: The implications are enormous.
items.exampleCN: 其影响十分巨大。

items.example: Are you implying that I lied?
items.exampleCN: 你是在暗示我撒谎吗？

items.example: There is an implicit warning in the letter.
items.exampleCN: 信里有隐含的警告。

items.example: The rules are explicit.
items.exampleCN: 规则写得明明白白。

definition_en: to suggest something without saying it directly, or to be a natural sign of something
core_image: 说话人眼神扫过空椅子，然后停在门口
scene: 介绍人没提任何名字，只说了句「位置还空着」。By saying the seat was empty, she implied that one of them was leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 imply 是「暗示」（第 1 个义项：不明说而让人领会），句意是她说座位空着，等于暗示其中一人要离开。画面里有扫过空椅子的眼神。

pos.zh: 动词：暗示、意味着、含有……的意思

senses.title: To suggest without saying
senses.definition: to make a listener understand something that is not spoken out
senses.definitionCN: 使听者领会未被说出的意思
senses.example: I did not mean to imply that you were wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 我并不想暗示你错了。
senses.why: The fold inside the Latin root explains it: the meaning is folded in, waiting to be opened by the listener.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根里的「折」正好解释：意思被折进去，等听者去展开。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: used of facts which logically point to a further fact
senses.definitionCN: 用于事实在逻辑上指向另一事实的情况
senses.example: The empty shelves imply a shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 空着的货架意味着短缺。
senses.why: Things imply each other as well as people, when one fact cannot stand without another behind it.
senses.whyCN: 不仅人，事物之间也互相蕴含：当一个事实离开背后的事实便站不住时。

senses.title: To involve as a necessary part
senses.definition: to bring something with it as a necessary condition
senses.definitionCN: 必然附带某条件或结果
senses.example: Taking the job implies moving to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 接下这份工作就意味着搬到另一座城市。
senses.why: A consequence folded into an action is implied by that action, so the verb also marks necessary conditions.
senses.whyCN: 折在行动里的后果由该行动所蕴含，于是这个动词也标示必要条件。

intro.en: Imply comes from the Latin verb for folding in, and English shaped it through French implication.
intro.cn: imply 来自拉丁语「折入」动词，英语形式经法语影响而定形。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and implicare to fold one thing into another.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，implicare 指把一物折进另一物。

items.en: French used emplier and later implied forms for wrapping a meaning inside words.
items.cn: 法语以 emplier 及后来的 implied 形式表示把含义包进言语。

items.en: English formed imply in the fourteenth century on the French model.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪仿法语模式造出 imply。

items.en: Logic gave the verb its technical sense: one statement implies another.
items.cn: 逻辑学赋予它专业义：一个陈述蕴含另一个陈述。

items.en: Everyday speech uses it constantly for polite hints and gentle accusations.
items.cn: 日常口语中它大量用于客气的暗示与委婉的指责。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fold family; the near-meaning group separates the confusable suggesting verbs.
note.cn: 形近组收「折叠」词族；近义组分辨几个容易混淆的「提示」动词。

entries.definition: The hinted meaning itself, as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 被暗示的意思本身，名词形式。

entries.definition: Folded in, understood without being stated.
entries.definitionCN: 折在其中、不待明说的。

entries.definition: To put to use, shaped like imply but from a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 应用、申请，形式与 imply 相似但前缀不同。

entries.definition: What the listener does with a hint, while imply is what the speaker does.
entries.definitionCN: 听者从暗示中推出；imply 是说着做的，infer 是听者做的。

entries.definition: To put an idea forward softly; wider than imply.
entries.definitionCN: 柔和地提出想法，比 imply 范围更广。

entries.definition: To have as a meaning, the plainest word in the group.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「意思是」，这组里最朴素的词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks pair imply with infer, and unfold the fold image into a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 imply 与 infer 配成一对，并把「折」的意象展开进句子里。

normal.en: The speaker implies, the listener infers; keep the direction straight.
normal.cn: 说者 imply，听者 infer，方向不能颠倒。

normal.en: Drop the e before -ed and -es: implied, implies.
normal.cn: -ed 与 -es 前要省掉 e：implied、implies。

normal.en: Two beats, stress the second: im-PLY.
normal.cn: 两个音节，重音在后：im-PLY。

normal.en: The plic fold hides inside, so the meaning is never on the surface.
normal.cn: '折'藏在里面，所以意思从不在表面上。

normal.en: As the name implies is a fixture of explanations and manuals.
normal.cn: as the name implies 是解释与手册里的常客。

abstract.en: The verb respects what silence can carry, since it lets a speaker act without saying.
abstract.cn: 这个动词尊重沉默所能承载的东西，让说者不必开口也能行动。

abstract.en: Facts imply too, and a good reader treats the world as a text folded in layers.
abstract.cn: 事实也会蕴含，好的读者把世界当作层层折叠的文本。

abstract.en: Accusations often travel through imply because it leaves no fingerprints.
abstract.cn: 指责常借 imply 传递，因为它不留指纹。

examples.en: The letter implies that the contract will not be renewed.
examples.cn: 这封信意味着合同不会续签。

examples.en: Are you implying that I made the mistake?
examples.cn: 你是在暗示是我的错吗？

examples.en: Silence does not imply agreement.
examples.cn: 沉默并不意味着同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + ply 折（plic 的变体）——把意思折进话里，不明说：暗示

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折叠」→ implicare「折入」，经法语影响，英语十四世纪造出 imply。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a polite hint, a sign in facts, and a necessary consequence.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：委婉的暗示、事实上的迹象，以及必然伴随的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker's glance at an empty chair, then at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话人瞥向空椅，又看向门口。

branches.en: THE HINT LINE: I did not mean to imply that is a common repair phrase.
branches.cn: 暗示线：我无意暗示……是常见的补救话。

branches.en: THE CLUE LINE: empty shelves imply shortage.
branches.cn: 线索线：空货架意味着短缺。

branches.en: THE CONDITION LINE: a job implies moving.
branches.cn: 条件线：一份工作意味着搬迁。

branches.en: THE PARTNER LINE: imply needs an inferring mind at the other end.
branches.cn: 搭档线：imply 需要另一端有一个在推断的心。

branches.en: THE LOGIC LINE: both are about what must follow.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：两者都关乎必然跟着来的东西。

intro.en: Imply is the verb of the fold family, with a dropped letter in its past forms and a noun in -ation.
intro.cn: imply 是「折叠」家族的动词，过去形式要省字母，名词以 -ation 收尾。

latinIntro.en: Implicare is Latin; the English verb was reshaped through French spelling habits.
latinIntro.cn: implicare 属拉丁语；英语动词形式受法语拼写习惯重塑。

items.example: Import begins with the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: import 前缀相同。

items.example: Reply and apply use the same shape.
items.exampleCN: reply 与 apply 形式相近。

items.example: The result implies more work.
items.exampleCN: 这一结果意味着更多工作。

items.example: The name implies great age.
items.exampleCN: 这名字意味着年头很久。

items.example: She implied nothing of the kind.
items.exampleCN: 她并没有那样的暗示。

items.example: He was implying more than he said.
items.exampleCN: 他话里有话。

items.example: The implication is serious.
items.exampleCN: 这个含义很严重。

items.example: The rule states it explicitly.
items.exampleCN: 规则里明确写了这一点。

definition_zh: 进口；引进；输入；（名词）进口品
definition_en: to bring goods into a country from abroad, or goods brought in this way
core_image: 码头上一排排从船腹里吊出来的集装箱
scene: 港口每天清早最忙，吊车一刻不停。The country imports most of its oil, so every delay on the shipping route is felt at the pumps.
sceneCN: 这里 import 是「进口」（第 1 个义项：把货物从国外运入本国），句意是这个国家的石油大多靠进口，因此航线上任何延误都会在加油站被感受到。画面里有码头上被吊起的集装箱。

pos.zh: 动词：进口、引进、输入
名词：进口、进口品

collocations.zh: 这一信息的分量（引申义）

senses.title: To bring goods in from abroad
senses.definition: to buy and bring goods into one's own country
senses.definitionCN: 从国外购入并把货物运入本国
senses.example: The factory imports steel from three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂从三个国家进口钢材。
senses.why: The prefix means into and the root means carry, so import is literally to carry in.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「向内」，词根意为「搬运」，所以 import 字面就是「向内搬运」。

senses.title: A good brought in
senses.definition: the goods or services brought into a country this way
senses.definitionCN: 以这种方式进入本国的货物或服务
senses.example: Imports rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年进口额大幅上升。
senses.why: The action and its object share one form in English, so the noun simply names what the verb brings.
senses.whyCN: 英语里动作与对象常共用一个形式，名词就直接指动词带进来的东西。

senses.title: The meaning or weight of words
senses.definition: the significance carried by a statement or event, a formal use
senses.definitionCN: 言语或事件所承载的意义，属正式用法
senses.example: Few understood the import of his words.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有人听懂他话里的分量。
senses.why: To carry is not only to move boxes; words and events carry meaning, and the old verb kept that freight sense.
senses.whyCN: 搬运不只运箱子，词与事件也承载意义，这个旧动词保留了这份「载重」之意。

intro.en: Import is a Latin verb for carrying in, and its shipping sense has survived unchanged for centuries.
intro.cn: import 是拉丁语「搬入」动词，其航运本义历经数百年未变。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, and importare meant to carry in or bring in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，importare 意为搬入、带入。

items.en: Trade Latin used importare for bringing goods into a province or a city.
items.cn: 商业用的拉丁语以 importare 指把货物运入行省或城市。

items.en: English took import at first for bringing in goods, and also for bringing in ideas.
items.cn: 英语最初用 import 指运入货物，也指引入观念。

items.en: Nation states and customs houses made import a fixed term of trade and duty.
items.cn: 民族国家与海关把 import 定为贸易与关税的固定术语。

items.en: The formal sense of weight or meaning kept the old freight metaphor alive.
items.cn: 表示「分量、含义」的正式用法让古老的「载重」比喻得以延续。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers carry-root words; the near-meaning group gathers trade words and their opposites.
note.cn: 形近组收「搬运」词根的词；近义组收贸易词及其对立词。

entries.definition: To carry goods out, the exact mirror of import.
entries.definitionCN: 把货运出去，正是 import 的镜像。

entries.definition: Easy to carry, from the same carrying root.
entries.definitionCN: 便于携带的，同出「搬运」之根。

entries.definition: Of great weight, built on the same freight idea.
entries.definitionCN: 很有分量的，同出「载重」之意。

entries.definition: The plain everyday phrase for importing.
entries.definitionCN: 进口的朴素日常说法。

entries.definition: To bring something in for the first time, often ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 首次引进，多指观念。

entries.definition: A load of goods sent, whether in or out.
entries.definitionCN: 运送的一批货，进出皆可。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the carry root, the in-out pair, and the freight of meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用上「搬运」词根、进出对立，以及意义的载重。

normal.en: Im- in, port carry: to carry in, and export is to carry out.
normal.cn: im- 向内，port 搬运：向内搬，而 export 是向外搬。

normal.en: The noun and verb look alike; the verb often stresses the second beat: im-PORT.
normal.cn: 名词动词同形；动词常重读第二拍：im-PORT。

normal.en: Port is also a harbour, where everything carried in arrives.
normal.cn: port 也是港口，正是向内搬运之物抵达之处。

normal.en: Important and import share the idea of weight carried.
normal.cn: important 与 import 共享「所载之重」这一意象。

normal.en: Imports come in, exports go out, and the e in export points outward.
normal.cn: imports 进、exports 出，export 的 e 指向外面。

abstract.en: Trade makes the word ordinary, but it began as pure carrying, and boxes and meanings both travel.
abstract.cn: 贸易让这个词变得平常，但它本只是搬运，箱子与意义都在旅途中。

abstract.en: A country that imports depends on ships it does not control.
abstract.cn: 进口国所依赖的船，未必由自己掌舵。

abstract.en: The formal sense reminds us that a sentence can carry freight too heavy for a careless listener.
abstract.cn: 那个正式义提醒我们：一个句子所载之重，粗心的听者扛不动。

examples.en: Britain imports much of its fruit from warmer countries.
examples.cn: 英国的水果大多从较温暖的国家进口。

examples.en: The tariff raised the price of imported cars.
examples.cn: 关税提高了进口汽车的价格。

examples.en: He spoke slowly, as if weighing the import of each word.
examples.cn: 他说得很慢，仿佛在掂量每个字的分量。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + port 搬（港口）——往本国港口搬货：进口；引申为含义所承载的分量

root: 拉丁语 portare「搬运」加向内前缀 in- 成 importare「搬入」，中世纪进入英语，近代定为贸易术语「进口」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: bringing goods in, the goods themselves, and the weight of a statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：把货运进来、所运进来的货物，以及话语所承载的分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: container boxes lifted out of a ship at dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨从船腹吊出的集装箱。

branches.en: THE TRADE LINE: countries buy what they cannot produce.
branches.cn: 贸易线：国家购买自己产不出的东西。

branches.en: THE STATISTIC LINE: imports appear in every trade report.
branches.cn: 统计线：进口额出现在每份贸易报告里。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE LINE: old prose still speaks of the import of words.
branches.cn: 语言线：旧体文章中仍说 the import of words。

branches.en: THE PORT LINE: harbours are where the verb and noun meet.
branches.cn: 港口线：港口正是动词与名词相遇之地。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT LINE: goods and words both arrive loaded.
branches.cn: 载重线：货物与语言都是载着重物抵达的。

intro.en: Import is a directional prefix on the Latin carrying root, with a mirror form in export.
intro.cn: import 是方向前缀加拉丁语搬运词根，export 是其镜像。

latinIntro.en: Portare and importare are recorded in Latin, and the root also builds portable and transport.
latinIntro.cn: portare 与 importare 均有拉丁文献，词根还造出 portable 与 transport。

items.example: Immigrant uses the same inward sense.
items.exampleCN: immigrant 也带同一向内之意。

items.example: Transport and portable share it.
items.exampleCN: transport 与 portable 共用此根。

items.meaning: to carry in; goods carried in
items.example: They import coffee from Brazil.
items.exampleCN: 他们从巴西进口咖啡。

items.example: The imported rice is cheaper.
items.exampleCN: 进口大米更便宜。

items.example: The firm began importing last spring.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司去年春天开始进口。

items.example: She is a wine importer.
items.exampleCN: 她是葡萄酒进口商。

items.example: The country exports machinery.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家出口机械。

items.example: It is an important meeting.
items.exampleCN: 这是一次重要的会议。

definition_en: the quality of being significant or mattering a great deal, and the weight that something carries in a particular situation
core_image: 地图上一个被红圈反复描了三圈的小城，旁边写着「务必拿下」
scene: 作战室里，参谋用红笔在地图上圈出一座小城，圈了三遍还嫌不够重。Everyone in the room understood the importance of that bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 importance 是「重要性、重大」（第 1 个义项：某事分量很重），句意是屋里每个人都明白那座桥的重要性。画面里有作战室、铺开的地图和反复描红的圈。

pos.zh: 名词：重要性、重要意义；重大

senses.title: The quality of mattering
senses.definition: the fact of being significant or affecting a lot
senses.definitionCN: 某事意义重大、影响很大的性质
senses.example: She never doubted the importance of a good night's sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不怀疑一夜好眠的重要性。
senses.why: This is the plain abstract sense: a thing has weight, and the noun names that weight.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的抽象义：一件事有分量，名词就把这个分量说出来。

senses.title: Significance in a situation
senses.titleCN: 在某情境中的重大意义
senses.definition: the special meaning that something has for a particular event or decision
senses.definitionCN: 某事物对某个事件或决定所具有的特殊意义
senses.example: The timing of the announcement was of great importance.
senses.exampleCN: 这次声明发布的时机极为重要。
senses.why: Here the weight is not general but attached to one decision, so the noun points to a particular stake.
senses.whyCN: 此时的分量不是泛泛而谈，而是压在某一个决定上，名词指向具体的利害。

senses.title: A sense of self-worth
senses.definition: a feeling that one matters more than others, often shown in a proud manner
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己比旁人重要的心态，常表现在傲气的举止上
senses.example: He speaks with a sense of his own importance.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话时总带着一种自视甚高的口气。
senses.why: The noun turns inward: importance becomes something a person claims for themselves.
senses.whyCN: 名词转向内部：importance 变成一个人替自己讨要的分量。

intro.en: Importance grows out of the Latin verb for carrying in, and its story moves from goods to meaning.
intro.cn: importance 出自拉丁语中「搬进来」的动词，它的故事从货物一路走到意义。

items.en: Importare was a compound of in and portare, to carry, and meant to bring in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 由 in 与 portare「搬运」合成，意为「搬进来」。

items.en: Importare also came to mean to carry meaning, to signify or matter, in legal and scholarly writing.
items.cn: 在中世纪的文书与学术写作里，它还引申出「含有意义、关系重大」的意思。

items.en: French formed importance from the same root, naming the weight that something carries.
items.cn: 法语从同一词根造出 importance，指事物所携带的分量。

items.en: English took importance in the sixteenth century, at first for significance in a statement or a matter.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 importance，最初指一段话或一件事的意义重大。

items.en: Later the word widened to cover personal standing, giving us the phrase a sense of one's own importance.
items.cn: 后来词义扩展到个人地位，于是有了「自视甚高」这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns for weight and value.
note.cn: 形近组收 import 这一家词；近义组收其他表示「分量、价值」的名词。

entries.definition: Goods brought in from abroad, or the act of bringing them in.
entries.definitionCN: 进口货物或进口这一行为，词根相同但侧重货物。

entries.definition: The adjective form, meaning mattering a great deal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，意为「重要的、重大的」。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used to stress a point in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，用来强调句中的某一点。

entries.definition: The meaning or value that something has, especially a hidden one.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「意义、重要性」，尤指隐含的意义。

entries.definition: The influence or force that something carries.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「分量、影响力」，借用物理重量说抽象地位。

entries.definition: The worth of something to the people who use it.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「价值」，指对使用者的用处与宝贵程度。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the carried-in root to how weight and meaning are assigned to things.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「搬进来」这一词根，连到人们如何给事物定分量、定意义这件事上。

normal.en: importance adds the noun ending -ance to the same root as import, so it is literally the weight something carries.
normal.cn: importance 就是在 import 同一词根上加名词词尾 -ance，字面就是事物所载的分量。

normal.en: The phrase of great importance is just a formal way to say very important.
normal.cn: of great importance 不过是 very important 的正式说法。

normal.en: Teachers often stress the importance of reading the whole text, meaning reading matters more than skimming.
normal.cn: 老师常说通读全文很重要，意思是通读比浏览更要紧。

normal.en: To attach importance to something is to hang a heavy tag on it.
normal.cn: attach importance to 某物，就是给它挂上一个很重的标签。

normal.en: A person who speaks of his own importance is carrying his own weight around loudly.
normal.cn: 口口声声说自己重要的人，是在到处大声扛着自己的分量。

abstract.en: Importance is not in the thing but in the network of plans around it.
abstract.cn: 重要性不在事物本身，而在围绕它铺开的那张计划之网里。

abstract.en: The word began with goods carried over a border and ended by carrying meaning.
abstract.cn: 这个词从跨越边界的货物开始，最后承运的是意义。

abstract.en: Everything is of importance to someone, and almost nothing is of importance to everyone.
abstract.cn: 任何事对某些人都重要，却几乎没有事对所有人都重要。

examples.en: The report stresses the importance of clean water in rural schools.
examples.cn: 报告强调了乡村学校清洁用水的重要性。

examples.en: It is a matter of great importance to the whole village.
examples.cn: 这对整个村子来说是一件极其重要的事。

examples.en: He speaks with an air of importance that amuses his colleagues.
examples.cn: 他说话时摆出一副了不起的样子，逗得同事们直乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: import 搬进来 + -ance 名词词尾——搬进来的东西越重，重要性越大

root: 由拉丁语 importare「搬进来」（in + portare「搬运」）经中世纪拉丁语「含有意义」的引申、法语 importance 进入英语，十六世纪起表示「意义重大」，后扩展到个人地位。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the general quality of mattering, the stake a thing has in one situation, and a person's proud sense of self-worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：泛指分量很重，在某具体情境中的分量，以及一个人自视甚高的架子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small town on a war map circled three times in red because everything depends on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一座小城被红笔圈了三遍，因为一切都系于它。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: importance is the general fact of mattering.
branches.cn: 性质线：importance 泛指「事情要紧」这一性质。

branches.en: THE STAKE: in one decision the word points to what can be lost.
branches.cn: 利害线：在具体决定中，这个词指向可能失去的东西。

branches.en: THE EGO: a sense of one's own importance is a claim to standing.
branches.cn: 自我线：自视重要，就是替自己讨要地位。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: of great importance dresses a plain adjective in formal clothes.
branches.cn: 搭配线：of great importance 给普通形容词换上了正式外衣。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: important and importantly carry the same weight in new forms.
branches.cn: 词族线：important 与 importantly 以新形式扛着同一个分量。

intro.en: The table shows the -ance noun ending on Latin roots and the family built on import.
intro.cn: 此表展示拉丁词根上的 -ance 名词词尾，以及以 import 为底的一族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb importare carries the in- prefix and the portare root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 importare 由前缀 in- 与词根 portare 组成。

items.example: Nobody questioned the importance of the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 没人质疑这次会议的重要性。

items.example: It is important to arrive on time.
items.exampleCN: 准时到达很重要。

items.example: More importantly, nobody was hurt.
items.exampleCN: 更重要的是，没有人受伤。

items.example: Skip the unimportant details in the summary.
items.exampleCN: 摘要里略去不重要的细节。

items.meaning: an exaggerated sense of one's worth
items.example: His self-importance made the meeting drag on.
items.exampleCN: 他自命不凡，害得会议拖了很久。

items.meaning: to bring goods in from abroad
items.example: The country imports most of its wheat.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家的小麦大部分靠进口。

items.example: A portable radio was all the news they had.
items.exampleCN: 他们能收到的新闻全靠一台便携收音机。

items.meaning: to carry across from one place to another
items.example: The goods are transported by rail.
items.exampleCN: 这些货物由铁路运输。

latinEntries.meaning: to bring in, to carry in
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：搬进来、输入
中世纪拉丁语名词：意义、分量

definition_zh: 重要的；重大的；有影响力的
definition_en: having a great effect or value, and therefore deserving attention, care, or respect
core_image: 一张被反复推到桌子正中央的纸条，上面写着「这件事必须做」
scene: 开工前的班前会上，班长把一张写着安全要求的纸推到桌子正中，拍了拍。Safety, he stressed, is the important part.
sceneCN: 这里 important 是「重要的、重大的」（第 1 个义项：分量重、必须重视），句意是班长强调，安全才是最要紧的那一部分。画面里有班前会、一张被推到桌子中央的纸条和班长的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：重要的、重大的；有影响力的

senses.title: Mattering a great deal
senses.definition: having a great effect or value, so that it deserves care and attention
senses.definitionCN: 影响或价值很大，因而值得用心对待
senses.example: Sleep is important for children who are still growing.
senses.exampleCN: 对还在长身高的孩子来说，睡眠很重要。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense: the thing carries weight and should not be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的义项：事情有分量，不能被忽略。

senses.title: Powerful or influential
senses.definition: having power or a high position in an organization or a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某个组织或领域里有权势、地位高
senses.example: She is an important figure in the city's music scene.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个城市的音乐圈里是个有分量的人物。
senses.why: The weight spreads from the matter to the person who controls it, so the adjective describes people too.
senses.whyCN: 分量从事延伸到掌握事的人身上，于是这个形容词也能形容人。

senses.title: Solemn or self-asserting
senses.definition: used of a tone or manner that treats small things as very serious
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种把小事故意当成大事的语气或神态
senses.example: He gave an important nod before opening the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他煞有介事地点了点头，才拆开信封。
senses.why: Once a word for weight, it can also describe someone who plays at carrying weight.
senses.whyCN: 原本说分量的词，也能形容装出分量的人。

intro.en: Important is the adjective of import, which comes from the Latin verb for carrying something in.
intro.cn: important 是 import 的形容词形式，而 import 源自拉丁语中表示「搬进来」的动词。

items.en: Importare joined in, into, with portare, to carry, and meant to bring something in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 把 in「进入」与 portare「搬运」组合起来，意为「把东西搬进来」。

items.en: Scholars used the verb for matters that carry meaning, so importare grew to mean to signify.
items.cn: 学者们用它来说「承载意义」的事，于是 importare 渐渐有了「意味着、关系重大」的意思。

items.en: French built the adjective important from the same stem, describing something of consequence.
items.cn: 法语由同一词干造出形容词 important，形容有后果、有关系的事物。

items.en: English adopted important in the sixteenth century, first in formal writing about serious matters.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 important，最初多见于谈论严肃事务的正式文章。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the adjective had spread into everyday speech and now covers people as well as things.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个形容词已进入日常口语，如今既能修饰事，也能修饰人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives with overlapping force.
note.cn: 形近组收 import 一族词；近义组收语义相近、强度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指「重要性」。

entries.definition: The adverb, used at the start of a sentence to add weight to a point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，常置于句首为某一点加重分量。

entries.definition: The verb and noun about bringing in goods from other countries.
entries.definitionCN: 指「进口」的动词与名词，与 important 同源但侧重货物。

entries.definition: Large enough to be noticed and to affect a result.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「显著的、有意义的」，强调大到能被察觉并影响结果。

entries.definition: So important that something cannot work without it.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「必不可少的」，强调缺了就根本不行。

entries.definition: Deciding the outcome at one particular point.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「关键的」，指在某个节点上决定结果。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the carried-in root and on the phrases that English has fixed around the adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕「搬进来」的词根，以及英语中已经固定下来的搭配来展开。

normal.en: important shares its root with import, and both are about what gets carried into the centre.
normal.cn: important 与 import 同根，说的都是被搬到正中央的东西。

normal.en: Make it a habit to say it is important to, followed by a verb in the base form.
normal.cn: 记住句型 it is important to 后面接动词原形。

normal.en: More important and most important take extra words rather than -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级和最高级用 more、most，而不是加 -er、-est。

normal.en: An important role is a part in a task that the task cannot do without.
normal.cn: an important role 就是任务里少了它就做不成的那一份。

normal.en: Someone who is important in a field is not just busy but has weight in decisions.
normal.cn: 在某个领域里重要的人，不只是忙，而是在决定中有分量。

abstract.en: Importance is assigned by plans: what a plan depends on becomes important.
abstract.cn: 重要性由计划分配：计划所依赖的东西就变得重要。

abstract.en: The same word covers the serious and the pompous, so tone does much of the work.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既说郑重，也说装样子，因此大半靠语气来区分。

abstract.en: Calling something important is a small act of power, since it decides what people look at.
abstract.cn: 说某件事重要，本身就是一种小小的权力，因为它决定了大家看什么。

examples.en: It is important to check the figures twice before publishing the report.
examples.cn: 公布报告前，把数据核对两遍很重要。

examples.en: Her grandmother played an important role in her education.
examples.cn: 她的祖母在她的教育中起了重要作用。

examples.en: He tried hard to look important while holding the small envelope.
examples.cn: 他拿着那个小信封，努力装出一副总揽大局的样子。

dict_mnemonic.text: import 搬进来 + -ant 形容词词尾——值得搬上台面的，就是重要的

root: 拉丁语 importare「搬进来」（in + portare「搬运」）经中世纪拉丁语「关系重大」的引申、法语 important 进入英语，十六世纪起用于正式书面语，后进入日常口语并扩展到形容人物地位。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: mattering a great deal, having power in a field, and a manner that treats small things as great.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：事情分量重，某人在领域内有分量，以及把小事故意做大的神态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slip of paper pushed to the centre of the table because everything today hangs on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸条被推到桌子正中央，因为今天的一切都系于它。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: important describes things that must not be ignored.
branches.cn: 分量线：important 形容不可忽略的事物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the adjective moves from matters to people with power.
branches.cn: 人物线：这个形容词从事转到有权势的人身上。

branches.en: THE ACT: an important nod is weight performed rather than carried.
branches.cn: 表演线：important 的一点头，是演出来的分量而非真分量。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: it is important to plus a verb is the most fixed frame.
branches.cn: 句型线：it is important to 加动词原形是最固定的框架。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: importance and importantly carry the same root into other word classes.
branches.cn: 词族线：importance 与 importantly 把同一词根带进别的词类。

intro.en: The table puts the -ant adjective ending next to the -ance and -ly forms of the family.
intro.cn: 此表把 -ant 形容词词尾放在同族的 -ance、-ly 形式旁边对照。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is importare, built from in and portare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 importare，由 in 与 portare 组成。

items.example: This letter is important, so keep it safe.
items.exampleCN: 这封信很重要，收好。

items.example: They spoke about the importance of honesty.
items.exampleCN: 他们谈到了诚实的重要。

items.example: Importantly, the whole team agreed.
items.exampleCN: 重要的是，全队达成了一致。

items.example: That is an unimportant detail for now.
items.exampleCN: 眼下那是个不重要的细节。

items.example: They import coffee from Brazil.
items.exampleCN: 他们从巴西进口咖啡。

items.meaning: to send goods out of a country
items.example: The firm exports machines to Africa.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司向非洲出口机器。

items.example: The beam supports the whole roof.
items.exampleCN: 这根梁支撑着整个屋顶。

items.example: A portable lamp lit the tent.
items.exampleCN: 一盏便携灯照亮了帐篷。

latinEntries.meaning: a harbour, a place where goods are carried in
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：港口，货物搬进之处

definition_zh: 重要地；重要的是；更为重要的是
definition_en: in a way that matters, used especially at the start of a statement to mark the point that deserves most attention
core_image: 一长串话讲完后，说话人抬起手指，把最后一句又说了一遍
scene: 会议上发言人讲完一堆数据，忽然抬起手，把最后一句又重复一遍。Importantly, no one lost money in the end.
sceneCN: 这里 importantly 是「重要的是」（第 1 个义项：用来标出最该听的那一点），句意是重要的是，最后没有人亏钱。画面里有会议室、一叠数据纸和一只抬起的手。

pos.zh: 副词：重要地；重要的是（用于强调某一点）

senses.title: Marking the key point
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a clause to single out the point that matters most
senses.definitionCN: 置于分句开头，挑出最该被听见的那一点
senses.example: Importantly, the medicine has no serious side effects.
senses.exampleCN: 重要的是，这种药没有严重的副作用。
senses.why: Here the adverb acts like a spotlight rather than describing how an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 此时副词像一束追光，而非描述动作怎么做的。

senses.title: Adding a weightier point
senses.titleCN: 更重要的是（追加更重的理由）
senses.definition: used with more or most to add a point that outweighs earlier ones
senses.definitionCN: 与 more、most 连用，补充一条压过前文的分量更重的理由
senses.example: The trip was cheap and, more importantly, safe.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行很便宜，更重要的是安全。
senses.why: The adverb now ranks reasons, telling the listener which one should be kept.
senses.whyCN: 此时副词在给理由排位次，告诉听者该记住哪一条。

senses.title: In a weighty manner
senses.definition: in a manner that suggests the speaker or doer takes themselves seriously
senses.definitionCN: 以一种自视甚重的神态行事
senses.example: He cleared his throat importantly before beginning.
senses.exampleCN: 他煞有介事地清了清嗓子才开始。
