senses.why: The old literal sense survives here: the adverb describes how something is done, not what is ranked.
senses.whyCN: 此处保留的是较早的字面义：副词描述做法神态，而不是给内容排位次。

intro.en: Importantly is the adverb of important, built on a Latin verb for carrying things in.
intro.cn: importantly 是 important 的副词，底子是拉丁语中「搬进来」的动词。

items.en: Importare combined in, into, and portare, to carry, giving the sense of bringing something in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 把 in「进入」与 portare「搬运」合起来，表示把东西搬进来。

items.en: The verb extended to meanings that carry weight, so to import came to mean to signify.
items.cn: 这个动词引申到「承载分量」的事上，to import 因而有了「意味着」的意思。

items.en: French formed important, and the -ment adverb that went with it.
items.cn: 法语造出 important，也造出了与它相配的 -ment 副词。

items.en: English made the adverb on its own pattern, adding -ly to important in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语按自己的构词方式，在十七世纪给 important 加上 -ly 做出副词。

items.en: The sentence-opening use, as in more importantly, spread in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 置于句首的用法，如 more importantly，到二十世纪才广泛流行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family; the near-meaning group gathers other spotlight adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组收 import 一族词；近义组收其他起「打光」作用的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective that stands before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，放在名词前。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指「重要性」。

entries.definition: With irritation at having to wait; a near neighbour in spelling only.
entries.definitionCN: 「不耐烦地」，与 importantly 拼写相近，意思无关。

entries.definition: Used to point out a fact worth noticing.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「尤其是、值得注意的是」。

entries.definition: Used to mark the point on which the outcome turns.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「关键是」，标出决定成败的那一点。

entries.definition: To a degree large enough to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「显著地」，指程度大到产生影响。

normalIntro.en: The hooks focus on the two live patterns: sentence-opening spotlight and the more importantly ranking.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子集中在两个活跃用法上：句首打光，以及 more importantly 的排位。

normal.en: Take important, add -ly, and put it at the front: the adverb becomes a spotlight.
normal.cn: important 加 -ly 放到句首，这个副词就变成一束追光。

normal.en: More importantly is a ranking signal: whatever follows beats whatever came before.
normal.cn: more importantly 是排位信号：后面的理由压过前面的。

normal.en: Most importantly is the last shot in a list, the one you want the reader to keep.
normal.cn: most importantly 是一串内容里的最后一枪，是希望读者记住的那一条。

normal.en: Equally importantly means the second reason weighs as much as the first.
normal.cn: equally importantly 表示第二条理由与第一条一样重。

normal.en: When it describes a manner rather than ranking, it sounds old-fashioned and slightly comic.
normal.cn: 当它描述神态而非排位时，听起来有点古旧，还带点滑稽。

abstract.en: Spotlight adverbs are a grammar of attention: they tell a listener where to spend memory.
abstract.cn: 这类打光副词是一套注意力语法，告诉听者该把记忆花在哪。

abstract.en: The word carries its history openly: it borrowed the weight of goods and now spends it on arguments.
abstract.cn: 这个词把历史明明白白地带着：它借来货物的重量，如今花在论证上。

abstract.en: Used too often, it loses its light, since everything cannot be the most important thing.
abstract.cn: 用得太频繁，它就会失去光亮，因为不可能每件事都最重要。

examples.en: Importantly, the new bus route reaches the hospital.
examples.cn: 重要的是，新公交线路通到医院。

examples.en: The plan is cheap and, more importantly, quick to carry out.
examples.cn: 这个方案花钱少，更重要的是执行得快。

examples.en: She nodded importantly and then said nothing at all.
examples.cn: 她煞有介事地点了点头，然后一个字也没说。

dict_mnemonic.text: important 重要的 + -ly 副词词尾——以「重要」的方式说出来，就是「重要的是」

root: 由 important 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；important 出自拉丁语 importare「搬进来」（in + portare「搬运」）经法语传入英语。句首强调用法在二十世纪广泛流行。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a spotlight at the start of a point, a ranking signal with more or most, and an old literal manner sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：句首点出重点，与 more、most 连用排位次，以及较古的「神态郑重」字面用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised finger repeating the last sentence because that is the one to keep.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抬起的手把最后一句话再说一遍，因为那才是要记住的。

branches.en: THE SPOTLIGHT: at the start of a clause it names the point that matters.
branches.cn: 追光线：置于分句开头时，它点出真正要紧的那一点。

branches.en: THE RANK: with more and most it orders reasons by weight.
branches.cn: 排位线：与 more、most 连用时，它按分量给理由排序。

branches.en: THE MANNER: describing a pompous way of acting keeps the old literal sense.
branches.cn: 神态线：形容做作的举止，保留的是较早的字面义。

branches.en: THE WRITING: in reports it marks what a reader should carry away.
branches.cn: 写作线：在报告里，它标出读者该带走的那句话。

branches.en: THE WARNING: overuse empties it, since every sentence cannot be the key one.
branches.cn: 警示线：滥用会掏空它，因为不可能每句都是关键句。

intro.en: The table shows how -ly turns adjectives into sentence adverbs and how the family hangs together.
intro.cn: 此表展示 -ly 如何把形容词变成句子副词，以及这一族词如何挂在一起。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin importare, from in and portare.
latinIntro.cn: 底子是拉丁语 importare，由 in 与 portare 组成。

items.meaning: in a way that marks what matters
items.example: Importantly, the door was left open.
items.exampleCN: 重要的是，那扇门一直开着。

items.example: An important letter arrived this morning.
items.exampleCN: 今天早上来了一封重要的信。

items.example: The importance of the find was clear at once.
items.exampleCN: 这一发现的重要性一眼就看得出来。

items.example: He was late and, more importantly, unprepared.
items.exampleCN: 他迟到了，更重要的是毫无准备。

items.meaning: to the same degree, a partner in the phrase equally importantly
items.meaningCN: 副词：同样地，可与 importantly 组成固定说法
items.example: The two rooms are equally warm.
items.exampleCN: 两个房间一样暖和。

items.meaningCN: 副词：尤其是、值得注意的是
items.example: Several guests, notably her aunt, arrived early.
items.exampleCN: 几位客人到得早，尤其是她姑妈。

items.example: They import steel for the yard.
items.exampleCN: 他们为船厂进口钢材。

items.meaningCN: 短语：说来也巧，也由同一副词构成
items.example: Importantly enough, the key was still in the lock.
items.exampleCN: 说来也巧，钥匙还插在锁上。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语分词：带有分量或意义的

definition_zh: 强加；征收（税费）；把……强加于
definition_en: to force a rule, tax, or burden on people, or to expect someone to accept something difficult without asking them
core_image: 一纸盖了红章的告示被人按在村口木门上，风一吹还在抖
scene: 村口木门上被人用图钉按住一张盖了红章的告示，风吹得纸边直抖。The town then imposed a new tax on every shop on that street.
sceneCN: 这里 impose 是「征收、强行施加」（第 3 个义项：把税费等硬按到别人身上），句意是镇上随后对那条街上的每家店铺都征收了一项新税。画面里有村口木门、图钉和一张被风吹得发抖的告示。

pos.zh: 动词：强加、强行施加（规则、负担、想法）；征收（税、罚金）

collocations.zh: 占用别人的时间、给人添麻烦
把自己的观点强加于人

derivatives.zh: （形近）给人深刻印象的、宏伟的
叠加、在……之上再加盖一层

senses.title: To force a rule on people
senses.definition: to officially force a law, rule, or limit on people who did not choose it
senses.definitionCN: 以官方力量把法律、规则或限制强加给没有选择余地的人
senses.example: The city imposed strict limits on fireworks during the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间，市里对燃放烟花实行了严格限制。
senses.why: The heart of the word is putting something on others with force, and rules are the most common burden.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「用力把东西压到别人身上」，而规则是最常见的负担。

senses.title: To force ideas or burdens on someone
senses.definition: to make someone accept your opinions, or to take up their time and patience
senses.definitionCN: 迫使别人接受你的看法，或占用他人的时间与耐心
senses.example: I do not want to impose my taste in music on the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 我不想把自己对音乐的品味强加给全家。
senses.why: The burden moves from laws to opinions and favours, which is why impose on means to be a nuisance.
senses.whyCN: 负担从法律挪到了看法与请求上，所以 impose on 才表示「给人添麻烦」。

senses.title: To charge a tax or fine
senses.definition: to order that a tax, duty, or punishment must be paid
senses.definitionCN: 下令让人必须缴纳某项税、关税或罚金
senses.example: A heavy duty was imposed on imported sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 对进口食糖征收了很高的关税。
senses.why: Taxation is the state at its most forceful, so this sense keeps the original physical pressure.
senses.whyCN: 收税是国家最用力的时候，所以这个义项仍保留着原始的身体性压强。

intro.en: Impose comes from Latin words for putting something down on top of something else, and the image of laying a burden on a person has survived.
intro.cn: impose 源于拉丁语中「把东西放到上面」的说法，而「把负担压在人身上」这个意象一直保留到今天。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and it underlies dozens of English verbs from compose to deposit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为「放置」，英语里从 compose 到 deposit 几十个动词都靠它。

items.en: Imponere added the prefix in, on, and meant to lay something upon or to place a burden on someone.
items.cn: imponere 加上前缀 in「在上」，意为把东西放上去，或把负担压在某人身上。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as imposer, used for laying on a charge or a duty.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成 imposer，多用于把什么责任或义务压在别人身上。

items.en: English borrowed it as imposen in the fourteenth century, first in the language of church and law.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，写作 imposen，最初多出现在宗教与法律用语里。

items.en: Later it covered taxes, opinions, and personal inconvenience, giving the modern phrase to impose on someone.
items.cn: 后来它的用法扩及征税、强加观点和给人添麻烦，于是有了现代短语 impose on someone。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the same ponere root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of forcing.
note.cn: 形近组收同样建在 ponere 词根上的动词；近义组收其他表示「强制」的动词。

entries.definition: To put something out where it can be seen, or to leave it open to harm.
entries.definitionCN: 「暴露、揭露」，同一词根，但前缀相反，方向朝外。

entries.definition: To put parts together into a whole, as in music or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 「组成、创作」，把部分摆到一起。

entries.definition: Grand and impressive in size or manner, from the same ing-form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「宏伟的、给人压迫感的」，是同一动词的 -ing 形式演变而来。

entries.definition: To make people obey a rule that already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「执行、实施」，指让已有的规则真正被遵守。

entries.definition: To make someone suffer something unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「使遭受（伤害、痛苦）」，强调让人承受痛苦。

entries.definition: To lay down what others must do, with no discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「发号施令、规定」，不容讨论地定下别人该做什么。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the put-on image behind the Latin root and the fixed English patterns with on.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用词根背后「放上去」的意象，以及英语中与 on 搭配的固定句式。

normal.en: impose is im plus pose, to put on, so a tax is literally placed on people.
normal.cn: impose 是 im 加 pose「放」，征税就是把税放在人身上。

normal.en: The verb nearly always takes on: impose a ban on, impose a tax on, impose on a friend.
normal.cn: 这个动词几乎总接 on：impose a ban on、impose a tax on、impose on a friend。

normal.en: Saying I do not want to impose is a polite way to admit you need a favour.
normal.cn: 说一句「我不想麻烦你」，是一种礼貌地承认自己要开口求人的方式。

normal.en: The adjective imposing looks like a burden but means grand, because a high wall puts weight on your eyes.
normal.cn: 形容词 imposing 看似负担，其实意为「宏伟」，因为高墙会在你眼前压下来。

normal.en: Keep the pair straight: impose means put on, expose means put out.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：impose 是往里压，expose 是往外摆。

abstract.en: Every rule imposes two costs: one on the person burdened and one on the person who must enforce it.
abstract.cn: 每条规则都强加两种代价：一种落在被管的人身上，一种落在必须执行它的人身上。

abstract.en: The word quietly records the direction of power, always downward from the strong to the weak.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄记下了权力的方向：永远从强者压向弱者。

abstract.en: A kindness offered unasked can still impose, which is why English keeps the phrase I hope I am not imposing.
abstract.cn: 未被请求的好意也可能构成麻烦，英语因此留有「希望我没有打扰你」这种说法。

examples.en: The government imposed new rules on drivers entering the city centre.
examples.cn: 政府对进入市中心的司机实行了新规定。

examples.en: Please stay for dinner; I hope I am not imposing.
examples.cn: 留下来吃晚饭吧，希望没给你添麻烦。

examples.en: Heavy fines were imposed on factories that poured waste into the river.
examples.cn: 向河里倾倒废料的工厂被处以重罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 在上 + pose 放——把东西硬放到别人身上，就是强加

root: 拉丁语 imponere「放在上面」（in「在上」+ ponere「放置」），经古法语 imposer 于中世纪英语时期进入英语，最初用于宗教与法律，后扩展到征税、强加观点与给人添麻烦。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: forcing rules, forcing opinions or inconvenience on people, and charging a tax or fine.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：强制推行规则，把想法或麻烦加给别人，以及征收税费或罚款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped notice pinned to a village gate, pressing its weight on everyone who walks through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖章的告示钉在村口木门上，把分量压在每个经过的人身上。

branches.en: THE RULE: a law is laid on people who never chose it.
branches.cn: 规则线：法律被压在从没选择过它的人身上。

branches.en: THE OPINION: taste and advice can be pressed on others just like rules.
branches.cn: 想法线：品味与忠告也能像规则一样压给别人。

branches.en: THE MONEY: a tax is the same pressure measured in currency.
branches.cn: 钱线：税收就是同一种压力用货币来计量。

branches.en: THE POLITENESS: I hope I am not imposing softens a request.
branches.cn: 礼貌线：一句「希望没有打扰你」，给请求垫上一层软话。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: imposition names the act, imposing describes the effect on the eye.
branches.cn: 词族线：imposition 指这个行为，imposing 则描述它落在眼里的效果。

intro.en: The table lines up verbs built on the Latin root ponere, put or place, with different prefixes.
intro.cn: 此表把以拉丁词根 ponere「放置」为底、带不同前缀的动词排在一起。

latinIntro.en: Ponere and its form pos- supply the spine of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: ponere 及其变体 pos- 是这一整组的脊梁。

items.meaning: to put a burden on others
items.example: They impose a small fee on every visitor.
items.exampleCN: 他们对每位访客征收一点费用。

items.meaning: the act of forcing something on people
items.example: The new imposition angered local traders.
items.exampleCN: 这项新的强制收费惹恼了当地商户。

items.meaning: to put something out in the open
items.example: The article exposed the hidden costs.
items.exampleCN: 那篇文章揭露了隐藏的费用。

items.example: She composed the song in one evening.
items.exampleCN: 她一个晚上就写好了这首歌。

items.example: He proposed a shorter working week.
items.exampleCN: 他提议缩短每周工时。

items.meaning: to put money down for safekeeping
items.example: Deposit the cheque at the counter.
items.exampleCN: 把支票存到柜台。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：宏伟的、气势逼人的
items.example: The imposing gate stopped us for a moment.
items.exampleCN: 那扇气势逼人的大门让我们愣了一下。

items.example: The imposed silence lasted a full minute.
items.exampleCN: 被强加的静默持续了整整一分钟。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：放在上面、施加

definition_zh: 不可能的；办不到的；难以忍受的
definition_en: not able to happen or be done at all, and, of a person or situation, extremely difficult to deal with
core_image: 一个人抱着梯子往一堵没有窗的墙顶上爬，墙后面还是同一面墙
scene: 工地上有人扛着梯子冲向一堵新砌的高墙，非要站到墙顶去，可墙后又是一模一样的墙。Getting the truck up that lane before noon looks impossible.
sceneCN: 这里 impossible 是「不可能的、办不到的」（第 1 个义项：根本没法发生或做到），句意是中午前让卡车开上那条小路看起来不可能。画面里有工地、扛梯子的人和两层一模一样的墙。

pos.zh: 形容词：不可能的、办不到的；（人、处境）难对付的

derivatives.zh: 不可能地；（用于强调）难以想象地
可能的（加否定前缀 in- 的变体 im- 构成反义）

senses.title: Cannot happen or be done
senses.definition: not able to happen or to be done under any realistic conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在任何现实条件下都无法发生或做到
senses.example: It is impossible to read the sign from that distance.
senses.exampleCN: 那个距离上根本看不清牌子。
senses.why: This is the plain sense: the thing lies outside what the world allows.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的义项：事情落在现实所允许的范围之外。

senses.title: Extremely hard to manage
senses.definition: used of a person or situation that refuses all reasonable handling
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人或处境怎么都处理不顺
senses.example: He is impossible before his first cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他喝第一杯茶之前谁都没法跟他打交道。
senses.why: The adjective slides from tasks to people, where impossible means stubborn rather than logically ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从任务滑到人身上，此时不可能指的是固执，而不是逻辑上被排除。

senses.title: So extreme it defies belief
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say something is extreme beyond what seems reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词前，表示程度极端到不合常理
senses.example: She came home at an impossible hour, long after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一个难以想象的钟点回了家，午夜已过很久。
senses.why: From cannot happen the word stretches to hardly believable, becoming an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 从「不能发生」引申到「难以置信」，这个词就成了程度加强词。

intro.en: Impossible is a negative form of possible, and possible itself goes back to a Latin verb for being able.
intro.cn: impossible 是 possible 的否定形式，而 possible 又出自拉丁语中表示「有能力」的动词。

items.en: Posse meant to be able, and its adjective possibilis described what can be done.
items.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为「能够」，其形容词 possibilis 用来形容可以做到的事。

items.en: In combination with the prefix in, impossibilis named what cannot be done at all.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 in 后，impossibilis 指完全做不到的事。

items.en: French carried the pair as possible and impossible, keeping the negative meaning intact.
items.cn: 法语把它当作 possible 与 impossible 这样一对词带着走，否定义保持不变。

items.en: English received both words in the fourteenth century, and impossible soon entered everyday argument.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪收下这两个词，impossible 很快就进了日常争辩里。

items.en: The looser uses of an impossible person and an impossible hour grew later, when the word started to express frustration.
items.cn: 「难对付的人」「难以想象的钟点」这类宽松用法是后来才长出来的，那时这个词开始承担不耐烦的情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the -ible family from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about being ruled out.
note.cn: 形近组收同词根下带 -ible 的一族词；近义组收其他表示「被排除」的形容词。

entries.definition: Able to happen or be done; the positive twin of the target word.
entries.definitionCN: 「可能的」，是 impossible 的肯定形式。

entries.definition: The adverb, often used to exaggerate, as in impossibly high.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，常用来夸张，如 impossibly high。

entries.definition: Making people admire it; a neighbour in spelling with a very different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 「令人印象深刻的」，拼写相近，意思完全不同。

entries.definition: Too terrible or absurd even to imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「不可想象的」，多指太可怕或太荒唐而不该想。

entries.definition: With no chance of success, and by extension very bad.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「无望的、没戏的」，也引申为「很差」。

entries.definition: Impossible to reach, though not impossible to imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「达不到的」，能想见却够不着。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the negative prefix and the patterns it fixes in English sentences.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用否定前缀，以及它在英语句子中固定下来的句式。

normal.en: The prefix im is the in- of negation reshaping itself before p, so impossible is simply not possible.
normal.cn: 前缀 im 是否定前缀 in- 在 p 前变形，所以 impossible 就是 not possible。

normal.en: English prefers it is impossible to plus a verb over saying a person cannot do it.
normal.cn: 英语更常说 it is impossible to 加动词，而不是直接说某人做不到。

normal.en: The frame make it impossible for someone to do something is standard in reports.
normal.cn: 「使某人无法做某事」这一框架在报告写作里已成标准。中译句式：使某人无法……

normal.en: Calling a colleague impossible says nothing about logic and everything about temper.
normal.cn: 说同事 impossible，说的是脾气，而不是逻辑。

normal.en: An impossibly steep road is not a road that cannot exist, just one that is too steep to believe.
normal.cn: an impossibly steep road 不是不存在，而是陡得难以相信。

abstract.en: Impossible is always relative to a set of tools, so it ages as fast as technology.
abstract.cn: impossible 总是相对于一套工具而言，因此它的岁数和技术更新一样快。

abstract.en: Saying something is impossible is sometimes a claim about courage rather than about the world.
abstract.cn: 说某事不可能，有时说的不是世界，而是勇气。

abstract.en: The word keeps a negative inside it, so double negatives make it positive again.
abstract.cn: 这个词体内带着否定，再用一次否定，它就重新变回肯定。

examples.en: It is impossible to please everyone in a class of forty.
examples.cn: 在一个四十人的班里让所有人都满意是不可能的。

examples.en: The rain made it impossible for us to see the mountain.
examples.cn: 下雨让我们根本看不见那座山。

examples.en: My uncle is impossible when he is hungry.
examples.cn: 我舅舅一饿就很难相处。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + possible 可能——不可能是可能的否定

root: 由否定前缀 in-（在 p 前变作 im-）加拉丁语 possibilis「能够做到的」构成，后者出自 posse「能」；经法语于十四世纪进入英语，后又引申出「难对付」「难以想象」等用法。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: unable to happen, unmanageable as a person or situation, and extreme beyond belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：无法发生或做到，人或处境难对付，以及程度极端到难以置信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder raised against a wall that has no window, with another identical wall behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：梯子架上墙，可墙上没有窗，墙后还是同样一面墙。

branches.en: THE WALL: impossible marks what the world does not allow.
branches.cn: 墙线：impossible 标出现实不允许的事。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: applied to people, it means unmanageable rather than ruled out.
branches.cn: 脾气线：用在人身上，指难对付，而非逻辑上被排除。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: impossibly turns the word into an intensifier.
branches.cn: 程度线：impossibly 把它变成加强词。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: possible is the positive twin, impossibility the abstract noun.
branches.cn: 词族线：possible 是肯定的一面，impossibility 是抽象名词。

branches.en: THE TOOL: each new tool moves the border between possible and impossible.
branches.cn: 工具线：每一件新工具都在挪动可能与不可能之间的边界。

intro.en: The table shows the -ible suffix and the way the negative prefix reshapes before p.
intro.cn: 此表展示 -ible 后缀，以及否定前缀在 p 前如何变形。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is posse, to be able, with the adjective possibilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 posse「能够」，及其形容词 possibilis。

items.example: That request is impossible to meet.
items.exampleCN: 那个要求没法满足。

items.example: A quick answer is possible today.
items.exampleCN: 今天就能给出答复。

items.example: No one argued the impossibility of the task.
items.exampleCN: 没人否认这任务不可能。

items.example: The room was impossibly small.
items.exampleCN: 那间房小得难以想象。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：看不见的，同一 -ible 模式
items.example: A thin wire is invisible from here.
items.exampleCN: 从这里看，一根细线是看不见的。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：难以置信的，同一模式
items.example: The rescue was an incredible feat.
items.exampleCN: 那次救援是惊人之举。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：非法的，否定前缀的另一种变体
items.example: Parking here is illegal.
items.exampleCN: 这里停车是违法的。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：不规则的，否定前缀在 r 前的变体
items.example: The verb has an irregular past form.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词的过去式是不规则的。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语形容词：能做到的
拉丁语形容词：做不到的

definition_zh: 给……留下深刻印象；使钦佩；使铭记
definition_en: to make someone feel admiration or respect by what you do, or to fix an idea firmly in someone's mind
core_image: 一块红蜡被人用力按在信封上，压出一个深深的印章图案
scene: 老邮局里，办事员把一块红蜡按在封口上，用力压出一个深凹的印章。She wanted to impress the examiner with a clear, confident answer.
sceneCN: 这里 impress 是「给……留下深刻印象」（第 1 个义项：做出让人佩服的样子），句意是她想以清晰自信的回答打动考官。画面里有老邮局、红蜡和压出的印章。

pos.zh: 动词：给……留下深刻印象、使钦佩；使铭记

collocations.zh: 使某人铭记、向某人强调

derivatives.zh: 令人印象深刻的、了不起的
不为所动的、没被打动的

senses.title: To make someone admire you
senses.definition: to make someone feel admiration by a performance, a quality, or an achievement
senses.definitionCN: 靠表现、品质或成就让人产生钦佩之情
senses.example: Her calm handling of the crisis impressed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她处理危机时的镇定让全队都很佩服。
senses.why: The physical pressure of the Latin root turns into an effect on the mind, as if a mark were pressed into someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根的身体性压强转成了对心思的作用，仿佛在别人心里压出一道印子。

senses.title: To fix something in the mind
senses.definition: to make someone remember an idea or duty very clearly
senses.definitionCN: 让某人牢牢记住某个道理或责任
senses.example: The coach impressed on us the need to warm up properly.
senses.exampleCN: 教练反复强调我们必须认真热身。
senses.why: Here the impression is knowledge rather than admiration, and English marks it with on.
senses.whyCN: 此时压进心里的不是钦佩而是知识，英语用 on 来标明这一层。

senses.title: To stamp a mark
senses.definition: to press a shape or a seal into clay, wax, or metal
senses.definitionCN: 把某个形状或图章压进黏土、蜡或金属里
senses.example: The seal was impressed into warm wax.
senses.exampleCN: 印章被压进了温热的蜡里。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal sense, from which the mental ones grew.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古、最字面的义项，心里的那几层都从这里长出来。

intro.en: Impress begins with the Latin verb for pressing something into a surface, and the mark left behind became a mental picture.
intro.cn: impress 起于拉丁语「把东西压进表面」的动词，而留下的印痕后来变成了心里的图象。

items.en: Premere meant to press, and it underlies English words from press to compress and suppress.
items.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为「压」，英语里 press、compress、suppress 都靠它。

items.en: Imprimere added the prefix in and meant to press into, to stamp a mark on a surface.
items.cn: imprimere 加上前缀 in，意为「压进去」，在表面压出印记。

items.en: French kept the verb as empreindre, and the noun impression for the mark left in wax or clay.
items.cn: 法语保留了动词 empreindre，名词 impression 则指留在蜡或黏土上的印痕。

items.en: English borrowed impress in the fourteenth century, still thinking of wax seals and printed marks.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 impress，那时想的还是火漆印章与印痕。

items.en: The mental sense grew in the seventeenth century, and to impress people with something became an everyday aim.
items.cn: 心里的那一层在十七世纪长出来，于是「用某样东西打动人」成了日常目标。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the press root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of arousing admiration.
note.cn: 形近组收以 press 为词根的动词；近义组收其他表示「引起钦佩」的动词。

entries.definition: The act of pressing meaning out, as in a look on the face or a phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 「表达、表情」，同一词根，方向是往外压。

entries.definition: The act of pressing something together to make it smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 「压缩」，把东西压得更小。

entries.definition: Not exact; a spelling neighbour that means almost the opposite of precise.
entries.definitionCN: 「不精确的」，拼写相近，与 precise 相反。

entries.definition: To make someone suddenly feel admiration or wonder, as in she struck me as honest.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「给人某种印象」，如某人给人以诚实的印象。

entries.definition: To change how someone thinks or acts without using force.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「影响」，不用强制地改变别人的想法或做法。

entries.definition: To fill someone with the urge or ability to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「鼓舞、激励」，让人心里生出做事的冲动。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the image of a seal pressed into wax and connect it to the two patterns with with and on.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子保留蜡上压印的意象，并把它连到 with 与 on 两种句式上。

normal.en: im plus press is pressing something in, so a good answer presses a little mark into the examiner's mind.
normal.cn: im 加压，就是把东西压进去，所以好答案会在考官心里留下一点印子。

normal.en: You are impressed by a thing, but you impress someone with it.
normal.cn: 你是被某事打动，而你是用某事打动别人。

normal.en: impress on someone keeps the old stamp sense: the lesson is pressed onto them.
normal.cn: impress on someone 保留着盖印的旧义：道理被压到人身上。

normal.en: impress and impression differ only in ending, just as print and its printed page differ.
normal.cn: impress 与 impression 只差词尾，就像印刷和印出的页面。

normal.en: Aim to impress is an old advice, yet nobody stays impressed by effort alone.
normal.cn: 「努力让人印象深刻」是句老话，可单靠努力也打动不了太久。

abstract.en: Every impression begins as physical pressure, and every social impression begins as someone pressing on you.
abstract.cn: 每一次印痕最初都是物理的压力，每一次社交印象最初也是有人在你身上用力。

abstract.en: The gap between what we intend to show and what stays in another mind is where impress lives.
abstract.cn: 我们想呈现的，和别人心里留下的之间那道缝，就是 impress 这个词活着的地方。

abstract.en: Institutions were stamped by seals, and private reputations are stamped by first meetings.
abstract.cn: 制度的信用盖在印章上，私人的名声盖在初次见面那一刻。

examples.en: He impressed the interviewers with his careful questions.
examples.cn: 他用细致的提问给面试官留下了深刻印象。

examples.en: The teacher impressed on us that a citation is a promise.
examples.cn: 老师反复叮嘱我们：引用文献是一种承诺。

examples.en: The metal plate was impressed with a pattern of leaves.
examples.cn: 金属板上压出了叶子的花纹。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 里面 + press 压——往心里压出印子，就是给人留下印象

root: 拉丁语 imprimere「压进去」（in + premere「压」），经法语 empreindre 于中世纪英语时期进入英语，先用于火漆与印版，十七世纪起引申为「在人心里留下印象」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: arousing admiration, fixing a lesson in someone's mind, and stamping a mark into a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：引起钦佩，把道理铭刻进人心，以及在表面上压出印记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red seal pressed hard into warm wax, leaving a deep shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：红蜡被用力压出一个深深凹陷的印子。

branches.en: THE WAX: the literal stamp is the root of the family.
branches.cn: 蜡线：字面上的压印是这一家词的根。

branches.en: THE ADMIRATION: the mark lands in someone's opinion of you.
branches.cn: 钦佩线：这道印子落在别人对你的看法里。

branches.en: THE LESSON: impress on presses a duty into memory.
branches.cn: 劝诫线：impress on 把责任压进记忆。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: impression and impressive are the noun and adjective of one act.
branches.cn: 词族线：impression 与 impressive 是同一动作的名词与形容词。

branches.en: THE FIRST SIGHT: a meeting works like a seal, and the mark stays.
branches.cn: 初遇线：一次初见就像盖印，印子留得很久。

intro.en: The table lines up words built on the Latin root premere, to press.
intro.cn: 此表把以拉丁词根 premere「压」为底的词排在一起。

latinIntro.en: Premere and its form press supply the shared spine of the group.
latinIntro.cn: premere 及其变体 press 是这一组的共同脊梁。

items.meaning: to press a mark in, to fill with admiration
items.example: The film impressed everyone in the room.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影让屋里所有人为之折服。

items.meaning: a mark or a feeling left behind
items.example: His first impression of the city was noise.
items.exampleCN: 他对这座城市的第一印象是吵闹。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：令人印象深刻的
items.example: The bridge is impressive at night.
items.exampleCN: 那座桥夜里很壮观。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：佩服的、被打动的
items.example: The judges were impressed by her poise.
items.exampleCN: 评委们对她的从容很欣赏。

items.example: Press the button twice.
items.exampleCN: 按两下按钮。

items.example: Compress the files before sending.
items.exampleCN: 发送前把文件压缩一下。

items.example: He could not suppress a smile.
items.exampleCN: 他忍不住笑了。

items.meaning: to press out, to put into words
items.example: She expressed her thanks simply.
items.exampleCN: 她简单地道了谢。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：压进去、盖印

definition_zh: 印象；感觉；印记；（书的）印数
definition_en: the idea or feeling you get about someone or something, and also the mark or the number of copies produced by printing
core_image: 刚走进一间陌生会议室时，第一眼看到的样子在脑子里留下的那张快照
scene: 推门进入面试的会议室，椅子的摆法、墙上的钟、说话人的语气，全在一瞬间被记住。My first impression of the office was that it felt calm and a little old.
sceneCN: 这里 impression 是「印象、感觉」（第 1 个义项：第一眼形成的感觉），句意是我对办公室的第一印象是安静、略带陈旧。画面里有刚推开的会议室门、墙上的钟和那一眼的快照。

pos.zh: 名词：印象、感觉；印记；印数、版次

derivatives.zh: 易受影响的、易被打动的

senses.title: The feeling you get
senses.definition: the idea or feeling that a person or thing produces in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物在你心里留下的看法与感觉
senses.example: The city gave me the impression of a place always in a hurry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市给我的印象是永远在赶时间。
senses.why: The mental sense grew from the physical mark, and it is now the most frequent use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 心理义从物理印痕长出来，如今已是这个词最常见的用法。

senses.title: A mark pressed into a surface
senses.definition: a shape or pattern pressed into wax, clay, or paper
senses.definitionCN: 在蜡、黏土或纸上压出的形状与纹样
senses.example: The ring left an impression in the soft wax.
senses.exampleCN: 戒指在软蜡上留下了一个印子。
senses.why: This is the original sense, still in use when the pressing is literal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的义项，当压的动作是真实的，它仍在使用。

senses.title: A printing run
senses.definition: all the copies of a book printed at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次印刷出来的全部书籍
senses.example: The first impression sold out within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次印刷的版本一个月内就卖完了。
senses.why: Printing presses leave marks on paper, so the word came to name one whole batch of marks.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机在纸上留下印子，于是这个词也用来指同一批印出来的东西。

intro.en: Impression is the noun partner of impress, and it names both the pressing and what the pressing leaves.
intro.cn: impression 是 impress 的名词伙伴，既指「压」这个动作，也指压出来的东西。

items.en: Imprimere meant to press into, and its noun impressio named the act and the mark.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imprimere 意为「压进去」，名词 impressio 既指动作又指印记。

items.en: The root premere, to press, also gave press and pressure, all sharing the same physical image.
items.cn: 词根 premere「压」还给出了 press 与 pressure，共用一个身体性意象。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as impression, still used for seal marks and prints.
items.cn: 古法语以 impression 沿用这个名词，多指印章与压出的图案。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, and printers soon used it for one run of copies.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，印刷商不久便用它指一次印刷的数量。

items.en: The modern mental sense took over in the eighteenth century, so that impressions are mostly felt rather than pressed.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，现代的心理义占了上风，如今印象多是感受到的，而不是压出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the impress family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a mental picture.
note.cn: 形近组收 impress 这一族词；近义组收其他表示「心里图像」的词。

entries.definition: The verb that produces an impression.
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，产生印象的那一方。

entries.definition: Deserving admiration because of size, skill, or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「令人印象深刻的」，因规模、技艺或效果而值得赞叹。

entries.definition: A word or look that carries meaning outward.
entries.definitionCN: 「表达、表情」，方向朝外，与前缀相反而对称。

entries.definition: An emotional state, often vaguer than an impression.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「感觉」，比 impression 更模糊、更偏情绪。

entries.definition: The way something is understood through the senses and the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「感知、看法」，强调经由感官与头脑的理解。

entries.definition: A picture held in the mind or presented to others.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「形象、图像」，指心里或对外的画面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the seal image and on the four fixed phrases English builds around the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕印章意象，以及英语中围绕这个名词固定下来的几种搭配。

normal.en: impression is impress with the noun ending -ion, so it is the mark that stays after the pressing.
normal.cn: impression 就是 impress 加名词词尾 -ion，是压完之后留下来的那个印子。

normal.en: Make a good impression is the phrase for first meetings, because the mark set early lasts.
normal.cn: make a good impression 是初次见面专用，因为早压下的印子留得久。

normal.en: Under the impression that means believing something wrongly, as if the mark were mistaken.
normal.cn: under the impression that 表示误以为，好像印子盖错了位置。

normal.en: In printing, the first impression is simply the first run off the press.
normal.cn: 印刷业里，the first impression 就是印机出来的第一版。

normal.en: Impressionism takes its name from a painting whose loose brushwork seemed to be only a first impression.
normal.cn: 印象派得名于一幅画，它松散的笔触看上去只像一次初见的印象。

abstract.en: An impression is a compression of another person into a small mental file.
abstract.cn: 印象就是把另一个人压缩成一份很小的心里档案。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that minds receive as wax receives: early marks are the deepest.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们，心接收的方式像蜡：越早压下的印子越深。

abstract.en: Between what is pressed on us and what we believe was pressed lies most of human misunderstanding.
abstract.cn: 别人压给我们的，和我们以为压过来的之间，横着人类大多数误会。

examples.en: First impressions are hard to change once they form.
examples.cn: 第一印象一旦形成就很难改变。

examples.en: I was under the impression that the shop closed at six.
examples.cn: 我一直以为这家店六点关门。

examples.en: The seal left a clear impression in the red wax.
examples.cn: 印章在红蜡上留下了清晰的印痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: impress 压印 + -ion 名词词尾——压在心上的那道印子，就是印象

root: 拉丁语 impressio「压入、印记」（imprimere 的名词），经古法语 impression 于中世纪英语时期进入英语；先指印章与印版，十八世纪起心理义「印象」成为主用法，印刷业中又指一次印量。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the feeling someone or something gives you, the physical mark, and one printing run of a book.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：人或事物给你的感觉，物理印痕，以及书籍的一次印量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mental snapshot taken in the first second of walking into a strange room.
core.cn: 核心意象：推开陌生房间门的头一秒，脑子里拍下的那张快照。

branches.en: THE FEELING: most impressions are now mental rather than physical.
branches.cn: 感觉线：如今多数印象是心理的，而非物理的。

branches.en: THE WAX: the physical mark keeps the oldest sense alive.
branches.cn: 蜡线：物理印痕让最老的义项继续活着。

branches.en: THE PRESS: a printing run is a batch of impressions on paper.
branches.cn: 印机线：一次印量就是纸上的一批印子。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: under the impression means holding a mistaken mark.
branches.cn: 搭配线：under the impression 表示心里盖着一个错的印象。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: impressionable describes a mind like soft wax.
branches.cn: 词族线：impressionable 形容一颗像软蜡一样的心。

intro.en: The table shows -ion nouns beside the verbs and adjectives of the same press family.
intro.cn: 此表把同一 press 家族的 -ion 名词与动词、形容词并排。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is imprimere, from in and premere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 imprimere，由 in 与 premere 组成。

items.meaning: a mark or a feeling left behind
items.example: The hall left a strong impression on her.
items.exampleCN: 那座大厅给她留下了强烈的印象。

items.meaning: to press in, to fill with admiration
items.example: The result impressed the judges.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果让评委们刮目相看。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：令人印象深刻的
items.example: She gave an impressive answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给出了一个令人赞叹的回答。

items.example: Children that age are highly impressionable.
items.exampleCN: 那个年纪的孩子很容易受影响。

items.meaning: the art movement named for a first impression
items.example: Impressionism changed how light was painted.
items.exampleCN: 印象主义改变了画家表现光线的方式。

items.meaning: an artist or performer of impressions
items.meaningCN: 名词：印象派画家；模仿艺人
items.example: The impressionist painted the river at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 那位印象派画家画了黎明的河。

items.meaning: pressing meaning out into words or looks
items.example: His expression gave nothing away.
items.exampleCN: 他的表情没透露任何信息。

items.meaning: a pressing down, of mood or of the land
items.example: The valley is a shallow depression.
items.exampleCN: 这片谷地是一个浅坑。

latinEntries.meaning: a pressing in, the mark left
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：压入，留下的印记

definition_zh: 令人印象深刻的；令人赞叹的；可观的
definition_en: so good, large, or skilful that people notice it and admire it
core_image: 一座横跨河面的大桥，桥索整齐排开，让人站在桥上忘了说话
scene: 第一次走上这座横跨河面的大桥，钢索整整齐齐排开，风里有回声。An impressive bridge, and the traffic was surprisingly quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 impressive 是「令人印象深刻的、令人赞叹的」（第 1 个义项：好到让人忍不住赞叹），句意是这是一座令人赞叹的桥，而且车流竟出奇地安静。画面里有横跨河面的大桥、整齐排开的钢索和风声。

pos.zh: 形容词：令人印象深刻的、令人赞叹的；（数量）可观的

derivatives.zh: 平平无奇的、不令人赞叹的

senses.title: Deserving admiration
senses.definition: so good or skilful that people admire it
senses.definitionCN: 好到或熟练到让人由衷赞叹
senses.example: Her command of three languages is impressive.
senses.exampleCN: 她掌握三种语言，令人佩服。
senses.why: The suffix -ive means having the power to do something, so impressive means able to impress.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 表示「具有……的力量」，所以 impressive 意为「能打动人的」。

senses.title: Large in scale
senses.definition: large enough in size or number to attract notice
senses.definitionCN: 在体量或数量上大到足以引人注目
senses.example: The library holds an impressive number of local maps.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆收藏的本地地图数量相当可观。
senses.why: Scale alone can create admiration, so the adjective also describes mere bigness.
senses.whyCN: 光是规模就能引发赞叹，所以这个形容词也能形容单纯的「大」。

senses.title: Making a strong effect
senses.definition: producing a strong visual or emotional effect, whether or not it is good in other ways
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉或情绪上造成强烈效果，别方面未必优秀
senses.example: The storm was impressive in its sheer noise.
senses.exampleCN: 那场暴风雨单凭声势就够惊人了。
senses.why: The word judges the strength of the effect, not always the quality behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词判的是效果有多强，而不是背后的品质一定多好。

intro.en: Impressive is built with the -ive suffix on impress, so it literally means having the power to press a mark into someone.
intro.cn: impressive 是在 impress 上加 -ive 后缀构成的，字面意思是「有力量在人心里压出印子的」。

items.en: Premere meant to press, and imprimere meant to press into, leaving a mark.
items.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为「压」，imprimere 意为「压进去」，留下印痕。

items.en: The suffix -ivus marked adjectives that describe a capacity or a tendency.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 用来标记表示能力或倾向的形容词。

items.en: French formed impressif along the same lines, keeping the sense of producing an effect.
items.cn: 法语按同样思路造出 impressif，保留「产生效果」的意思。

items.en: English took impressive in the sixteenth century, at first for things that leave a strong mark on the mind.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 impressive，最初指能在人心里留下强烈印痕的事物。

items.en: Praise broadened its use, so that impressive now covers size, skill, and sheer spectacle.
items.cn: 赞美的用法把它推得更广，如今可形容规模、技艺，也可形容纯粹的场面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in form; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of praise.
note.cn: 形近组收外形相近的词；近义组收表示赞许的形容词。

entries.definition: Feeling admiration, said of the person rather than the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 「被打动的」，说的是人而不是物，容易与 impressive 混用。

entries.definition: The feeling or mark that is left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指留下的感觉或印痕。

entries.definition: Able to show feeling clearly, from the opposite prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 「富有表现力的」，前缀相反，方向朝外。

entries.definition: Unusual enough to catch the eye at once.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「醒目的、引人注目的」，强调一眼就被抓住。

entries.definition: Worth talking about because it is unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「非凡的」，因不寻常而值得议论。

entries.definition: Extremely beautiful, grand, or splendid.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「壮丽的、宏伟的」，侧重华美与气派。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the difference between the thing that impresses and the person who is impressed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住「打动人的东西」与「被打动的人」之间的区别。

normal.en: impressive ends in -ive, which marks the power to act: the thing itself does the impressing.
normal.cn: impressive 以 -ive 收尾，标记的是「有力量去作用」，是事物本身在打动人。

normal.en: You are impressed; the bridge is impressive. Change the ending to change who feels what.
normal.cn: 你是 impressed，桥是 impressive，换个词尾就换了谁在感受。

normal.en: In praise, impressive is the safe middle ground: stronger than good, weaker than extraordinary.
normal.cn: 在赞美里，impressive 是稳妥的中段：比 good 强，比 extraordinary 弱。

normal.en: Numbers can be impressive too, as in an impressive collection of stamps.
normal.cn: 数量也能令人赞叹，比如一份相当可观的邮票收藏。

normal.en: Unimpressive is the quiet way to say a thing failed to move you at all.
normal.cn: unimpressive 是委婉地说某样东西完全没打动你。

abstract.en: What counts as impressive shifts with the crowd, so praise always carries a reference group inside it.
abstract.cn: 什么叫令人赞叹随人群而变，所以每次赞许里都藏着一个参照群体。

abstract.en: The suffix says the object has force of its own, which is why we rarely call a borrowed achievement impressive.
abstract.cn: 后缀说这事物本身带着力量，所以我们很少说借来的成就令人赞叹。

abstract.en: Impressive is the vocabulary of selection: it ranks what deserves to be remembered.
abstract.cn: impressive 是筛选用的词，它给「值得被记住」排了队。

examples.en: The team made impressive progress in only six weeks.
examples.cn: 这支队伍仅用六周就取得了令人瞩目的进展。

examples.en: We were impressed by how calmly she answered.
examples.cn: 她回答得如此镇定，让我们很佩服。

examples.en: The storm was impressive, though it did little damage.
examples.cn: 那场暴风雨声势惊人，不过没造成什么破坏。

dict_mnemonic.text: impress 使留有印象 + -ive 形容词词尾——能给人压出深印的，就是令人印象深刻的

root: 在拉丁语 imprimere「压进去」的英语动词 impress 之上加形容词后缀 -ive（表示「具有……力量」），经法语 impressif 于十六世纪进入英语，词义由「能在心上留印」扩展到规模与场面。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: deserving admiration, large in scale, and strong in effect on the eye or the ear.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：值得赞叹，规模可观，以及在视听上造成强烈效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bridge whose cables are so orderly that people stop talking when they step on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座钢索排列齐整的大桥，人一踏上去就忘了说话。

branches.en: THE SKILL: impressive marks something done unusually well.
branches.cn: 技艺线：impressive 标出做得格外好的东西。

branches.en: THE SIZE: sheer quantity can carry the same weight.
branches.cn: 规模线：光是数量也能扛起同样的分量。

branches.en: THE FORCE: a storm can impress without being good.
branches.cn: 力量线：一场暴风雨可以不带善意地令人惊叹。

branches.en: THE PAIR: impressed belongs to the person, impressive to the thing.
branches.cn: 对照线：impressed 归人，impressive 归事物。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: impressively and unimpressive turn the same stem to adverb and negation.
branches.cn: 词族线：impressively 与 unimpressive 把同一词干变成副词与否定。

intro.en: The table puts -ive adjectives beside the verbs and nouns they come from.
intro.cn: 此表把 -ive 形容词与其来源的动词、名词放在一起。

latinIntro.en: The Latin -ivus tagged a capacity, and it survives in dozens of English adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 -ivus 标记的是能力，它在英语里留下了几十个形容词。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：令人印象深刻的
items.example: The hall was impressive in its size.
items.exampleCN: 那座大厅之大令人惊叹。

items.meaning: in a way that earns admiration
items.example: She finished the race impressively fast.
items.exampleCN: 她跑完比赛的速度令人赞叹。

items.example: We were impressed by the careful work.
items.exampleCN: 那份细致的活让我们很佩服。

items.example: The lobby was clean but unimpressive.
items.exampleCN: 大堂很干净，但无甚出彩。

items.example: Her expressive face told the whole story.
items.exampleCN: 她那张表情丰富的脸说明了一切。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：有吸引力的，同一 -ive 模式
items.example: The garden is attractive in spring.
items.exampleCN: 这个花园春天很迷人。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：决定性的、果断的
items.example: It was a decisive moment for the club.
items.exampleCN: 那对俱乐部来说是决定性的时刻。

items.example: Early impressions often survive correction.
items.exampleCN: 早期的印象往往即使被纠正也还在。

latinEntries.meaning: having the nature or power of
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语后缀：具有……性质或力量
拉丁语形容词：有压印之力的

definition_en: to make something better, or to become better in quality, condition, or skill
core_image: 一块粗糙的木料被刨子一遍遍推过，表面一点点变平变亮
scene: 木工房里，老师傅推着刨子，一次一次从粗木板上削下薄薄一层。Keep practising and your handwriting will improve within a month.
sceneCN: 这里 improve 是「改进、变好」（第 1 个义项：质量或状况向好的方向变化），句意是坚持练习，一个月内你的字就会变好。画面里有木工房、刨子和一层层削下的木花。

pos.zh: 动词：改进、改善；提高（技能、产量）；好转

collocations.zh: 在……基础上更进一步、胜过

derivatives.zh: 有启发性的、使人进步的

senses.title: To make something better
senses.definition: to make a thing or a condition better than it was
senses.definitionCN: 把事物或状况变得比原来更好
senses.example: The council improved the drainage along the main road.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门改善了主干道沿线的排水。
senses.why: Here the verb takes an object: someone acts on something and raises its quality.
senses.whyCN: 此时动词带宾语：有人对某物施加作用，把它的品质提高。

senses.title: To become better
senses.definition: to grow better by itself, as a skill, a health condition, or a result
senses.definitionCN: 技能、健康状况或结果自行变好
senses.example: Her reading improved a lot after a summer of daily practice.
senses.exampleCN: 坚持一个暑假的每日练习后，她的阅读进步了很多。
senses.why: With no object, the change happens to the subject, and English does not need a separate verb for it.
senses.whyCN: 不带宾语时，变化发生在主语身上，英语不需要另造动词。

senses.title: To do better than before
senses.definition: used with on to say a new attempt beats an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 与 on 连用，表示新的尝试超过了旧的
senses.example: The second design improves on the first in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 第二个设计在每个细节上都胜过第一个。
senses.why: Improve on marks comparison rather than repair, so the earlier version stays as a measure.
senses.whyCN: improve on 指向比较而非修补，旧的版本因此成了一根标尺。

intro.en: Improve began in French as a word about turning a profit, and only later became the general word for making better.
intro.cn: improve 最初是法语中关于「获利」的词，后来才成为泛指「变好」的词。

items.en: En prou was a phrase meaning into profit, used of land or trade that produced gain.
items.cn: 古法语的 en prou 意为「进入收益之中」，用于能产生利润的土地或买卖。

items.en: The verb emprouwer grew from it, meaning to turn to profit, to make land yield more.
items.cn: 动词 emprouwer 由此长成，意为「使之有利可图」，让土地多出产。

items.en: English borrowed it as improwen in the fifteenth century, first in farming and estate accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入，写作 improwen，最初见于农事与庄园账目。

items.en: The sense widened from land to anything: a house could be improved, then a method, then a person.
items.cn: 词义从土地扩展到一切：房屋可以改善，方法可以改善，人也可以改善。

items.en: The spelling settled as improve, and the older money sense now survives only in the phrase improve the occasion.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 improve，较早的「获利」义如今只留在少数固定说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words beginning with the same im- shell; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of getting better.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 im- 开头的词；近义组收其他表示「变好」的动词。

entries.definition: To agree officially to something, a completely different act.
entries.definitionCN: 「批准、赞同」，与 improve 只差一个字母，意思毫不相干。

entries.definition: The noun for the change or the thing that was changed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指改进这件事或改进之处。

entries.definition: Better than before, used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，放在名词前表示「改良过的」。

entries.definition: To raise the value or appeal of something already good.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「提升、增强」，让本来就不错的东西更有价值。

entries.definition: To replace something with a better model or version.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「升级」，用更好的型号或版本替换。

entries.definition: To remove small faults by careful repeated work.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「精炼、打磨」，靠细致反复的工作去掉小毛病。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the farming origin of profit and the three patterns the verb takes with and without an object.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用它「获利」的农事出身，以及动词带宾语与不带宾语的几种句式。

normal.en: Improve began as a word for making land yield more, so better and more profitable still sit close together.
normal.cn: improve 起初是说让土地多出产，所以「更好」和「更有利」至今挨得很近。

normal.en: It works with or without an object: you improve a text, and the text improves.
normal.cn: 它既可带宾语也可不带：你改进一篇文章，文章也会变好。

normal.en: Improve on means beat, so the new version is not repairing the old one but beating it.
normal.cn: improve on 意思是胜过，新版本不是在修旧的，而是在赢过它。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with approve, which means giving permission for something.
normal.cn: 别与 approve 混淆，那个词是「批准」。

normal.en: The noun improvement keeps the -ment of result, so an improvement is the thing left after the work.
normal.cn: 名词 improvement 带 -ment 表示结果，所以改进之处就是干完活剩下的东西。

abstract.en: Improvement assumes a scale: nothing is better without a standard to be better than.
abstract.cn: 改进预设了一把尺子：没有可比的旧标准，就谈不上更好。

abstract.en: The word carries its commercial past, which is why improving land and improving profits sound so natural.
abstract.cn: 这个词扛着商业出身，所以「改良土地」和「提高利润」听来一样自然。

abstract.en: Small daily improvements compound, while grand rewrites often collapse.
abstract.cn: 每天的小改进会累积，而大改造常常垮掉。

examples.en: Reading aloud every day will improve your pronunciation.
examples.cn: 每天朗读会改善你的发音。

examples.en: The roads improved noticeably after the new budget passed.
examples.cn: 新预算通过后，路况明显好转。

examples.en: No one has improved on her record in twenty years.
examples.cn: 二十年来没人打破过她的纪录。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 进入 + prove 利益——让它进入更好的收益里，就是改进

root: 源自古法语 en prou「进入收益之中」及动词 emprouwer「使之有利可图」，十五世纪进入英语，最初用于农事与庄园账目，后泛指「改好、提高」，现代义已覆盖技能、状况与设计。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: making something better, becoming better by itself, and beating an earlier version.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：把某物改好，自身变好，以及在比较中胜过旧版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plane shaving a rough board thinner and thinner until it shines.
core.cn: 核心意象：刨子一趟趟从粗木板上削下木花，直到板面发亮。

branches.en: THE HAND: with an object, improve is work done on something.
branches.cn: 动手线：带宾语时，improve 是对某物做的功夫。

branches.en: THE GROWTH: without an object, the change belongs to the subject.
branches.cn: 成长线：不带宾语时，变化归主语自己所有。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: improve on ranks a new version above an old one.
branches.cn: 比较线：improve on 把新版本排在旧版本之上。

branches.en: THE FARM: the oldest sense made land yield more.
branches.cn: 农事线：最老的义项是让土地多出产。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: improvement and unimproved mark the result and its absence.
branches.cn: 词族线：improvement 与 unimproved 标出成果与未改进。

intro.en: The table shows how -ment and -ed turn this verb into a result and a description.
intro.cn: 此表展示 -ment 与 -ed 如何把这个动词变成结果与描述。

latinIntro.en: The verb is not Latin but Old French, built from the phrase en prou, into profit.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词并非来自拉丁语，而是古法语中由 en prou「进入收益」构成的。

items.example: They improve the soil with compost.
items.exampleCN: 他们用堆肥改善土壤。

items.meaning: the change or the better part
items.example: The new roof is a real improvement.
items.exampleCN: 新屋顶确实是一大改进。

items.example: The improved engine uses less fuel.
items.exampleCN: 改进后的发动机更省油。

items.example: The talk was improving for the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 那场讲话对全班都有启发。

items.example: The unimproved meadow is full of wild flowers.
items.exampleCN: 那片未改良的草地里满是野花。

items.meaning: to give official consent, a false friend
items.example: The board approved the budget.
items.exampleCN: 董事会批准了预算。

items.meaning: to show something to be true
items.meaningCN: 动词：证明，拼写相近但不同源
items.example: He proved the point with two examples.
items.exampleCN: 他用两个例子证明了这一点。

items.meaning: an act of changing position, same -ment pattern
items.example: The movement of the crowd was slow.
items.exampleCN: 人群移动得很慢。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 古法语短语：进入收益之中
古法语动词：使之有利可图

latinEntries.meaning: to be useful, a Latin cousin of profit

definition_en: the act of making something better, or a change that makes something better than before
core_image: 同一段路前后对比：左边坑坑洼洼，右边新铺的柏油在阳光下泛光
scene: 村口那条土路修好之后，孩子们推着车跑得飞快，不再怕下雨天。Someone said the road had seen no improvement in twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 improvement 是「改进、改善」（第 1 个义项：让情况变好的改变），句意是新排水系统是这些年来学校最大的一处改变。画面里有修好的村路、推车跑过的小孩和新铺的柏油。

pos.zh: 名词：改进、改善；改进之处；进步

senses.title: The act of making better
senses.definition: the process of making something better in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使事物在质量或状况上变好的过程
senses.example: The improvement of the water supply took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 供水系统的改善花了两年时间。
senses.why: The -ment suffix names the action itself, so this sense is about the work rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: -ment 后缀指的是动作本身，所以这一义项说的是功夫，而不是结果。

senses.title: A change that makes things better
senses.definition: one particular change that makes a place, plan, or product better
senses.definitionCN: 某一处让地方、计划或产品变得更好的具体改动
senses.example: A second window was the only improvement the room needed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间唯一需要改的就是再加一扇窗。
senses.why: From the process the noun turns countable and points to a single piece of work done.
senses.whyCN: 名词从过程变为可数，指向具体做成的某一处。

senses.title: Getting better in health or skill
senses.definition: the way a person's condition or ability gets better over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的状况或能力随时间变好的过程
senses.example: The doctor saw a slow improvement in his breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生看到他的呼吸在慢慢好转。
senses.why: The subject here is a person, so improvement describes recovery or growth rather than repair.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，所以 improvement 指的是康复或长进，而非修补。

intro.en: Improvement comes from the same French root as improve, which once meant turning something to profit.
intro.cn: improvement 与 improve 同源，都出自法语，原意是「使之有利可图」。

items.en: En prou meant into profit, and the verb emprouwer meant to make land yield more.
items.cn: 古法语 en prou 意为「进入收益」，动词 emprouwer 意为让土地多出产。

items.en: The noun formed on the same stem with the -ment ending that marks a result.
items.cn: 名词由同一词干加表示结果的 -ment 词尾构成。

items.en: English took it as improvement, first used for the work known as land improvement.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 improvement，最初指今天仍称「土地改良」的那种活。

items.en: As the verb widened, the noun followed, covering buildings, methods, skills, and health.
items.cn: 随着动词义扩展，名词也跟着扩展，涵盖房屋、方法、技能与健康。

items.en: The plural improvements became the usual way to speak of separate works done to a place.
items.cn: 复数 improvements 成了指同一处地方所做的几项不同工程时的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the improve family and its false friends; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns of progress.
note.cn: 形近组收 improve 一族词及易混词；近义组收其他表示「进步」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb that carries out the change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，负责做出改变。

entries.definition: The same -ment ending on a different verb, meaning a shift of position.
entries.definitionCN: 同一 -ment 词尾接在另一个动词上，意为「移动」。

entries.definition: Official consent, from approve, which differs from improve by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: 「批准」，出自 approve，与 improve 只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Forward movement toward a goal over time.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「进展」，指朝着目标向前推进。

entries.definition: A change to a better model or a higher class.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「升级」，换成更好的型号或更高档次。

entries.definition: A planned change to a system that is thought to be faulty.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「改革」，针对被认为有缺陷的制度所做的改变。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the -ment result ending and on the fixed phrases that treat improvement as a countable gain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕表示结果的 -ment 词尾，以及把改进当成「可数收获」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Add -ment to improve and you get the thing done, just as a payment is the thing paid.
normal.cn: improve 加 -ment 得到「做成的结果」，就像 payment 是付出去的那笔钱。

normal.en: Room for improvement is the polite phrase for work still undone.
normal.cn: room for improvement 是委婉地说「还有活没干」。

normal.en: Make improvements to a place means leave it better than you found it.
normal.cn: make improvements to 一个地方，就是把那里弄得比来时更好。

normal.en: In medicine and sport, improvement is usually uncountable: a slow improvement, not an improvement of two.
normal.cn: 在医学和运动语境里，improvement 通常不可数，只说「慢慢好转」。

normal.en: Do not mix it with approval; one letter changes a better road into a signed form.
normal.cn: 别和 approval 搞混，差一个字母，路变好了就成了签字盖章。

abstract.en: The word once meant profit from land, and it still measures gain against what a place used to yield.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指从土地获利，如今仍在用「从前出产多少」来衡量增益。

abstract.en: Countable improvements are promises kept one by one, and they are what voters and patients actually feel.
abstract.cn: 可数的改进是一条条兑现的承诺，也是选民和病患真正感受到的东西。

abstract.en: Because it compares with the past, improvement can never be declared in the present tense alone.
abstract.cn: 因为它是和过去相比，所以改进不能只靠现在时来宣布。

examples.en: There has been a clear improvement in air quality this winter.
examples.cn: 今年冬天的空气质量有了明显改善。

examples.en: The essay is good but there is room for improvement in the last paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇文章不错，不过最后一段还有改进余地。

examples.en: Watering the garden was the only improvement the new tenant asked for.
examples.cn: 给花园装浇水设备是新房客唯一提出的改进。

dict_mnemonic.text: improve 改进 + -ment 名词词尾——改进这件事或改进之处

root: 与 improve 同源，出自共同源于古法语的构词（en prou「进入收益」），名词形式先在英语中出现（improvement），最初指对土地与庄园所做的改良，后泛指建筑、方法、技能与健康方面的改善。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the work of making better, one particular better change, and a person's recovery or growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：改进这件事，某一处具体的改动，以及人在健康或技能上的好转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two versions of the same road, one rutted and one freshly paved.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路的前后两版，一版坑洼，一版刚铺好柏油。

branches.en: THE WORK: improvement names the work done, often uncountable.
branches.cn: 工夫线：improvement 指所做的工夫，常为不可数。

branches.en: THE ITEM: made countable, it is one finished better thing.
branches.cn: 条目线：变成可数时，就是一处做好的改动。

branches.en: THE PERSON: for people it means recovery and growth.
branches.cn: 人身线：用在人身上，指康复与长进。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: room for improvement softens criticism.
branches.cn: 搭配线：room for improvement 把批评说软了。

branches.en: THE FARM: the land origin still shows in phrase like land improvement.
branches.cn: 农事线：改良土地这类说法里仍看得见它的出身。

intro.en: The table compares -ment nouns of result with the verbs that produce them.
intro.cn: 此表把表示结果的 -ment 名词与其来源动词放在一起比较。

latinIntro.en: The verb is Old French rather than Latin, though -ment itself came from Latin -mentum.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词来自古法语而非拉丁语，但 -ment 本身出自拉丁语 -mentum。

items.meaning: the act or the better thing
items.example: The new lights are a small improvement.
items.exampleCN: 新灯算是一点小改进。

items.example: These exercises improve balance.
items.exampleCN: 这些练习能改善平衡。

items.example: A sudden movement scared the bird.
items.exampleCN: 一个突然的动作吓到了那只鸟。

items.meaningCN: 名词：成就，同一 -ment 模式
items.example: Finishing the course was a real achievement.
items.exampleCN: 读完这门课确实是件成就。

items.meaningCN: 名词：协议，同一 -ment 模式
items.example: They reached agreement in an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们一小时内达成了协议。

items.example: The lessons had an improving effect.
items.exampleCN: 这些课有使人进步的作用。

items.meaning: one who or that which improves
items.example: Soil improver is added before planting.
items.exampleCN: 种植前会加土壤改良剂。

items.example: The unimproved lane is still muddy.
items.exampleCN: 那条没修过的小路还很泥泞。

latinEntries.meaning: a suffix naming the result of an action
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语后缀：表示动作的结果

latinEntries.meaning: to make better, the Latin cousin of the idea
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：使变好，表示同一概念的拉丁表亲

definition_en: the state of not being able to do something, usually because of a lack of power, skill, or a chance
core_image: 一双手被绑在身后，面前是一扇明明没锁却推不开的门
scene: 志愿队赶到山里的第二天，担架不够，医生的手再稳也抬不动那么多人。His inability to speak the local language made the first week very slow.
sceneCN: 这里 inability 是「无法、没有能力」（第 1 个义项：因为缺条件而做不成），句意是他不会说当地话，头一周进展极慢。画面里有山里的医疗点、一双稳当的手和担架。

pos.zh: 名词：无能力、无法（做某事），常与 to do 或 to 名词连用

collocations.zh: 对自己无能为力的沮丧

derivatives.zh: 能力（加否定前缀 in- 构成反义）

senses.title: Lacking the power to do something
senses.definition: the fact of not being able to do something because the power or skill is absent
senses.definitionCN: 因为缺少力量或技能而做不到某件事
senses.example: The disease causes a gradual inability to walk.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病会导致逐步无法行走。
senses.why: The noun names a state rather than an act, so it usually appears with a following to-clause or noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指一种状态而非动作，所以通常跟一个 to 加动词或名词的说明。

senses.title: Not being allowed or unable by circumstance
senses.definition: the position of being unable to act because of money, rules, or other outside limits
senses.definitionCN: 因钱、规定或其他外部限制而无法行动
senses.example: Their inability to pay the rent was the real cause of the move.
senses.exampleCN: 他们无力付房租才是搬家的真正原因。
senses.why: Here the lack is not in the person but in the situation, and the noun describes that pressure.
senses.whyCN: 此时缺的不是人的本事，而是条件，名词描述的是那种压强。

senses.title: A particular weakness
senses.definition: one specific thing a person or a system cannot do well
senses.definitionCN: 人或系统在某个具体方面做不好
senses.example: The report lists the company's inabilities without much softening.
senses.exampleCN: 报告直白列出了这家公司的短处。
senses.why: Made countable, the noun points to individual gaps rather than a general state.
senses.whyCN: 变成可数后，名词指向一项项具体的缺口，而不是总体状态。

intro.en: Inability is the negative of ability, and both rest on a Latin word for being skilful or fit.
intro.cn: inability 是 ability 的否定形式，两者都建在拉丁语中表示「能干、合适」的词上。

items.en: Habere meant to hold, and habilis described something easy to hold or handle, hence handy and fit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 habere 意为「持握」，形容词 habilis 形容好用、好拿，引申为「合适、能干」。

items.en: The noun habilitas named the quality of being fit for a task, especially in law about rights.
items.cn: 名词 habilitas 指适合做某事的资格，尤用于法律中关于权利的说法。

items.en: French reshaped it as habilite, then ablete, meaning skill or competence.
items.cn: 法语把它改作 habilite，又作 ablete，意为技能与胜任之力。

items.en: English took ability in the fourteenth century, and inability followed quickly as its plain opposite.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪收下 ability，inability 作为其朴素的反面很快跟上。

items.en: Medicine and law made inability a formal word for a lasting loss of power or of a legal right.
items.cn: 医学与法律把 inability 变成正式用词，指能力或法律资格的持续缺失。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the -ility family; the near-meaning group gathers words for lacking power.
note.cn: 形近组收 -ility 一族词；近义组收表示「缺少力量」的词。

entries.definition: The positive twin, meaning skill or the power to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式「能力、才能」，是 inability 的正对面。

entries.definition: A tendency to change or fall over, not a lack of skill.
entries.definitionCN: 「不稳定」，指容易变化或失衡，并非缺少技能。

entries.definition: The state of not noticing or not caring.
entries.definitionCN: 「不敏感、不体谅」，同为 in- 加 -ility 的构造。

entries.definition: The feeling of having no control over events.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「无力感」，强调对局面毫无掌控。

entries.definition: A formal word for being unable, often because of health or law.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「无行为能力」，正式用语，多因健康或法律原因。

entries.definition: A lack of success in doing something actually attempted.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「失败」，指尝试了却没成功，与「做不到」有别。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the negative prefix and the sentence frames that inability almost always appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用否定前缀，以及 inability 几乎总出现在其中的句式。

normal.en: in plus ability makes it clear: take the skill away and you get inability.
normal.cn: in 加 ability 一目了然：把本事拿走，剩下的就是 inability。

normal.en: Inability almost always takes to: inability to sleep, to pay, to read.
normal.cn: inability 后面几乎总接 to：inability to sleep、to pay、to read。

normal.en: It is a state, not a failed attempt, so it is not the same as failure.
normal.cn: 它是一种状态，而不是一次失败的尝试，所以不等于 failure。

normal.en: Hospitals and contracts prefer inability because it sounds neutral and lasting.
normal.cn: 医院与合同偏爱 inability，因为它听起来中性且指较持久的情形。

normal.en: When you want the adjective instead of the noun, use unable to do.
normal.cn: 如果要形容词而不是名词，就用 unable to do。

abstract.en: Naming an inability is usually a first step in asking for help, which is why the word sounds quietly honest.
abstract.cn: 说出「做不到」往往就是求援的第一步，所以这个词听来有种安静的诚实。

abstract.en: The root for ability meant easy to hold, so ability is always about fitting a task, not about being better in the abstract.
abstract.cn: ability 的词根意为「好拿」，所以能力始终是说「适合某项任务」，而非抽象地更强。

abstract.en: Most social inabilities are misnamed; what is called inability is often a lack of permission.
abstract.cn: 许多所谓「做不到」其实是被叫错了名字，真正缺的常是许可，而非能力。

examples.en: His inability to remember names embarrasses him at parties.
examples.cn: 他记不住名字，在聚会上常为此尴尬。

examples.en: The village's inability to reach a doctor was solved by a mobile clinic.
examples.cn: 村里看病难的问题靠一辆流动诊所解决了。

examples.en: She spoke openly about her inabilities as a young teacher.
examples.cn: 她坦率谈起自己当年轻老师时的种种短板。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 不 + ability 能力——能力被拿走的状态，就是「做不到」

root: 由否定前缀 in- 加 ability 构成；ability 出自拉丁语 habilitas「适合做某事的资质」，源自 habilis「好持握、灵巧」，经古法语进入中世纪英语，inability 随之出现，后成为医学与法律中的正式用词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: lacking power or skill, being blocked by outside conditions, and one particular weakness.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：缺本事，被外部条件卡住，以及某一方面的具体短处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands tied behind the back in front of an unlocked door that will not open.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手被绑在身后，面前是一扇没锁却推不开的门。

branches.en: THE SKILL: the missing thing may be training or strength.
branches.cn: 本事线：缺的可能是训练，也可能是力气。

branches.en: THE MEANS: money and rules can produce the same state.
branches.cn: 条件线：钱和规定也能造出同样的状态。

branches.en: THE LIST: plural inabilities itemise separate gaps.
branches.cn: 清单线：复数形式把短板一项项列出来。

branches.en: THE FRAME: inability to do something is the fixed pattern.
branches.cn: 句式线：inability to do something 是固定框架。

branches.en: THE PAIR: ability and inability stand on the same Latin root.
branches.cn: 对照线：ability 与 inability 站在同一拉丁词根上。

intro.en: The table shows -ility nouns built on -able adjectives and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: 此表展示由 -able 形容词派生的 -ility 名词，以及否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is habilis, from habere, to hold.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 habilis，出自 habere「持握」。

items.meaning: the state of not being able
items.example: His inability to swim kept him on the shore.
items.exampleCN: 他不会游泳，只能待在岸上。

items.example: Her ability to listen is rare.
items.exampleCN: 她善于倾听，这在人里少见。

items.example: He was unable to answer.
items.exampleCN: 他答不上来。

items.meaning: the power to do a larger task
items.meaningCN: 名词：能力、性能，同 -ility 模式
items.example: The printer has a colour capability.
items.exampleCN: 这台打印机具备彩色输出能力。

items.example: The wall needs stability at the base.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙底部需要稳定支撑。

items.example: There is a possibility of snow.
items.exampleCN: 有可能下雪。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：不敏感的、不体谅的
items.example: That was an insensitive remark.
items.exampleCN: 那句话很不体谅人。

items.meaningCN: 名词：不作为，同为 in- 加名词
items.example: Inaction cost them the contract.
items.exampleCN: 不作为让他们丢了合同。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语形容词：好拿、灵巧的
拉丁语名词：适合做某事的资质

definition_zh: 英寸；一点点的距离；缓慢移动
definition_en: a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot, about two and a half centimetres, and by extension a very small distance or a slow movement
core_image: 尺子被拉到刻度上，拇指正好压住第十二道最细的那一格
scene: 裁缝把布边掀起，用拇指抵住尺子上的第十二小格做记号。The shelf was a few inches longer than the wall, so it had to be cut down.
sceneCN: 这里 inch 是「英寸」（第 1 个义项：长度单位，一英尺的十二分之一），句意是架子比墙长了几英寸，只好锯短。画面里有裁缝的拇指、尺子上最细的那一格和一块布边。

pos.zh: 名词：英寸；（引申）极小的距离
动词：一点一点地移动

derivatives.zh: 尺蠖（一伸一缩像在量寸的毛毛虫）

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.definition: a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot, about 2.54 centimetres
senses.definitionCN: 长度单位，等于一英尺的十二分之一，约二点五四厘米
senses.example: The screen is eleven inches wide.
senses.exampleCN: 这块屏幕宽十一英寸。
senses.why: The word begins as a measure, and the measure comes from the width of a thumb.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一个度量，而度量来自拇指的宽度。

senses.title: A very short distance
senses.definition: used figuratively for a small gap or a small margin
senses.definitionCN: 比喻说法，指很小的距离或很小的余量
senses.example: The rail missed the post by an inch.
senses.exampleCN: 铁轨差一点就撞上柱子。
senses.why: Because an inch is short, the word becomes a figure for near-misses and tiny margins.
senses.whyCN: 因为一英寸很短，这个词就成了「险些」与「微小余量」的象征。

senses.title: To move very slowly
senses.definition: to move forward in tiny steps, as traffic or a difficult process does
senses.definitionCN: 像车流或艰难进程那样，以极小步幅向前挪
senses.example: The queue inched along the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍沿着走廊一点点往前挪。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to advance one inch at a time is to inch along.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了动词：一次前进一英寸，就是 inch along。

intro.en: Inch is one of the oldest words in English for measuring, and it began as the width of a thumb.
intro.cn: inch 是英语中最古老的度量词之一，起初就是「一个拇指宽」。

items.en: Ynce meant the twelfth part of a foot, borrowed early from Latin uncia.
items.cn: 古英语 ynce 指一英尺的十二分之一，很早就从拉丁语 uncia 借来。

items.en: Uncia meant a twelfth part, used both for the inch and for the Roman ounce.
items.cn: 拉丁语 uncia 意为「十二分之一」，既用于英寸也用于罗马的盎司。

items.en: Old laws defined the ynce as three barleycorns laid end to end, a thumb-wide measure.
items.cn: 古法规定一英寸等于三颗大麦粒首尾相接，也就是一个拇指的宽度。

items.en: The spelling settled as inch, and the word entered proverbs about small gains and slow progress.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 inch，并进入了关于「积少成多」与「缓慢前进」的谚语。

items.en: The verb to inch appeared in the nineteenth century, formed straight from the noun.
items.cn: 动词 to inch 在十九世纪出现，直接由名词转成。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short nouns and verbs that look similar; the near-meaning group gathers other length units.
note.cn: 形近组收外形相近的短词；近义组收其他长度单位。

entries.definition: An annoying feeling on the skin that makes you want to scratch.
entries.definitionCN: 「痒」，与 inch 只差一个字母，完全是另一回事。

entries.definition: Coloured liquid used for writing and printing.
entries.definitionCN: 「墨水」，读音接近，拼写更短。

entries.definition: To squeeze skin tightly between two fingers.
entries.definitionCN: 「捏、掐」，是 inch 加了一个起首辅音。

entries.definition: A unit of length of twelve inches.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「英尺」，等于十二英寸。

entries.definition: A metric unit of length, about two fifths of an inch.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「厘米」，约合五分之二英寸。

entries.definition: A unit of length of thirty-six inches.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「码」，等于三十六英寸。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the thumb-width origin to the phrases and the verb that grew out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「拇指宽」的出身，连到由它长出的短语和动词上。

normal.en: An inch is the width of a thumb, so the word is a body measurement in disguise.
normal.cn: 一英寸就是一个拇指的宽度，所以这个词其实是一次身体量度。

normal.en: Twelve inches make one foot; that twelve is why Latin gave it the name for a twelfth part.
normal.cn: 十二英寸是一英尺，正因这个十二，拉丁语才管它叫「十二分之一」。

normal.en: Inch by inch is the phrase for progress so slow you could measure it with a ruler.
normal.cn: inch by inch 形容慢到能用尺子量出来的进展。

normal.en: Every inch of the room means the entire room, not just the measurements.
normal.cn: every inch of the room 指整个房间，而不只是量尺寸。

normal.en: As a verb, inch needs a direction word: inch forward, inch towards the door.
normal.cn: 作动词时 inch 后面要跟方向词：inch forward、inch towards the door。

abstract.en: A unit taken from the body disappears when the metric system spreads, yet the mental picture lasts.
abstract.cn: 来自身体的单位会随公制推广而消退，可心里的那个画面还在。

abstract.en: Small units are the vocabulary of near misses, because we only count tiny margins when they matter.
abstract.cn: 小单位是「险些」的词汇，因为只有在意时我们才去数那一点点余量。

abstract.en: The same word measures cloth and measures patience, since traffic inching along is patience made visible.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量布，也量耐心，因为车流一点一点挪动正是耐心的可见形态。

examples.en: The old photo is only three inches across.
examples.cn: 这张老照片只有三英寸宽。

examples.en: She missed the bus by an inch, or rather by a second.
examples.cn: 她差点就赶上那趟公交，其实就差一秒。

examples.en: The car inched forward through the flooded street.
examples.cn: 汽车在被淹的街道上一点点向前挪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 英寸 = 一个拇指的宽度，十二个拇指是一英尺

root: 古英语 ynce 借自拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」，古法规定一英寸为三颗大麦粒首尾相接、约合一个拇指宽；中世纪英语拼作 inch，十九世纪由名词转化为动词，表示「缓慢移动」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the unit itself, a tiny distance used figuratively, and the verb for moving very slowly.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：长度单位本身，比喻用法中的极短距离，以及缓慢移动的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thumb pressed on the twelfth smallest mark of a ruler.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指按在尺子上第十二道最细的刻线上。

branches.en: THE RULER: the unit is still the everyday measure of cloth and screens.
branches.cn: 尺线：这个单位至今是量布与量屏幕的日常尺度。

branches.en: THE MARGIN: an inch is the figure for a near miss.
branches.cn: 余量线：一英寸成了「险些」的象征。

branches.en: THE CRAWL: as a verb it measures how slowly something goes.
branches.cn: 爬行线：作动词时，它量的是东西走得有多慢。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: every inch means the whole thing, not a measure.
branches.cn: 搭配线：every inch 指整体，不是量值。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENCE: inch is a body measure, centimetre is a decimal one.
branches.cn: 对照线：英寸是身体量度，厘米是十进制度量。

intro.en: The table gathers short measuring words and the verb forms inch makes.
intro.cn: 此表汇集短小的度量词，以及 inch 变出的动词形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor is uncia, a twelfth part, which also gave ounce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语祖先是 uncia「十二分之一」，也是 ounce 的来源。

items.example: The nail is two inches long.
items.exampleCN: 这颗钉子有两英寸长。

items.example: The gap is six inches wide.
items.exampleCN: 这条缝有六英寸宽。

items.example: The train inched into the station.
items.exampleCN: 列车缓缓驶入车站。

items.example: Inching along, they reached the top at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 他们一点点挪，到黄昏才登顶。

items.meaning: a caterpillar that moves by looping
items.example: An inchworm crossed the leaf.
items.exampleCN: 一只尺蠖爬过叶子。

items.meaning: a weight unit; both words come from a word for a twelfth part
items.meaningCN: 名词：盎司，与英寸同出「十二分之一」
items.example: Add an ounce of butter.
items.exampleCN: 加一盎司黄油。

items.example: The board is a foot wide.
items.exampleCN: 这块板一英尺宽。

items.example: They bought two yards of cloth.
items.exampleCN: 他们买了两码布。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：十二分之一

latinEntries.meaning: the Roman ounce, one twelfth of a pound
latinEntries.meaningCN: 罗马盎司，一磅的十二分之一
拉丁语名词：拇指，也是一种身体量度

definition_zh: 事件；事故；（不严重的）插曲
definition_en: something that happens, especially something unusual or unpleasant, or a single small event inside a larger one
core_image: 街角的路灯下，一只打翻的牛奶瓶和一地碎玻璃被警用黄带围了起来
scene: 清晨街角的路灯下，一只牛奶瓶翻倒在地，碎玻璃散了一小片。The police wrote down every detail of the incident before the street filled up.
sceneCN: 这里 incident 是「事件、事故」（第 1 个义项：发生的、多带负面意味的事情），句意是警察在街上人多起来之前记下了这起事件的所有细节。画面里有路灯、打翻的牛奶瓶和一小片碎玻璃。

pos.zh: 名词：事件、事故；（较大的事情中的）一件小事、插曲

collocations.phrase: at the scene of the incident

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: an event, especially one that is unusual, unpleasant, or worth reporting
senses.definitionCN: 一件事情，尤指不寻常的、不愉快的或值得上报的事
senses.example: The school recorded three similar incidents last term.
senses.exampleCN: 学校上学期记录了三起类似事件。
senses.why: The word names a happening in the world, and English uses it most for things that disturb the normal order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指世上发生的某件事，而英语最常用它来说打破常态的事情。

senses.title: A small episode inside a larger one
senses.definition: one small event that forms part of a longer story, journey, or process
senses.definitionCN: 构成一段较长经历、旅程或过程的一件小事
senses.example: The lost ticket was a minor incident in an otherwise calm journey.
senses.exampleCN: 丢车票只是这趟平顺旅程中的一个小插曲。
senses.why: Here the word orders events inside a narrative rather than warning of trouble.
senses.whyCN: 此时这个词是在叙述里给事件排位置，而不是警示有麻烦。

senses.title: An accident or clash
senses.definition: an accident, a fight, or a clash between groups, as reported by officials
senses.definitionCN: 官方通报中的意外事故、打斗或群体冲突
senses.example: A border incident nearly led to talks breaking down.
senses.exampleCN: 一起边境冲突差点让谈判破裂。
senses.why: Official language fixed the word on accidents and clashes, especially in police and military reports.
senses.whyCN: 官方语言把这个词固定在事故与冲突上，尤其在警务与军事报告中。

intro.en: Incident comes from a Latin verb for falling upon, and the idea of something that falls into your path still shapes it.
intro.cn: incident 出自拉丁语中表示「落在上面」的动词，而「落到你路上来的东西」这一意象至今仍在起作用。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it underlies English words from accident to cadence and chance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为「落下」，accident、cadence、chance 都从它而来。

items.en: Incidere added the prefix in and meant to fall upon, as events fall upon a person.
items.cn: incidere 加前缀 in，意为「落在上面」，就像事情落在一个人身上。

items.en: The participle incidens was used as a noun for a happening, a thing that falls upon us.
items.cn: 分词 incidens 被用作名词，指落在我们身上的一件事。

items.en: French formed incident with the same sense of an event, often an unlucky one.
items.cn: 法语造出 incident，同样指一件事，且多指不走运的事。

items.en: English took it in the fifteenth century, and reporting language made it the standard word for accidents and clashes.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入，通报语言又把它定成事故与冲突的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same falling root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for happenings.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「落下」词根下的词；近义组收其他表示「事情」的词。

entries.definition: An unexpected harm nobody intended, from the same Latin verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 「意外、事故」，同一词根不同前缀，强调无人故意。

entries.definition: How often something occurs across a group or a period.
entries.definitionCN: 「发生率」，讲的是频次而不是单件事。

entries.definition: By the way; used to add a side remark.
entries.definitionCN: 副词「顺便说一下」，用来补一句旁枝的话。

entries.definition: Anything that happens, usually planned or at least neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「事件」，中性，常指安排好的事情。

entries.definition: One part of a longer story or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「一段插曲」，是较长故事或病程中的一节。

entries.definition: A fact of something happening, often noted in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「发生的事」，多见于统计与记录。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the falling image behind the root and the fixed phrases of official reports.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用词根背后「落下」的意象，以及通报中的固定搭配。

normal.en: An incident is something that falls on you; accident is the same fall with a different prefix.
normal.cn: incident 是落到你身上的事；accident 是同一种「落」，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Without incident is the phrase for a journey that went exactly as planned.
normal.cn: without incident 形容一趟完全按计划走完的行程。

normal.en: Police write incident reports, which is why the word so often means something bad.
normal.cn: 警察写的是 incident report，所以这个词多半指不好的事。

normal.en: Incidentally means by the way, so a side event turned into a formula for changing subject.
normal.cn: incidentally 意为「顺便一提」，一件旁枝之事变成了改话题的套话。

normal.en: Keep the pair straight: an incident is one case, incidence is how often it happens.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：incident 是一件事，incidence 是发生的频率。

abstract.en: Naming something an incident is already a judgement that it is small enough to be handled.
abstract.cn: 把一件事称作 incident，本身就是在判断它小到可以处理。

abstract.en: The word carries a fall inside it, so every incident carries a hint of things going out of control.
abstract.cn: 这个词体内装着「落下」，所以每起事件都暗示着事物失去控制。

abstract.en: Reports choose the noun, and the noun sets the size: an incident rarely becomes a crisis on paper.
abstract.cn: 报告在挑选名词，名词也在设定大小：在纸上，事件很少升级为危机。

examples.en: The flight landed without incident despite the storm.
examples.cn: 尽管有暴风雨，航班还是平安落地。

examples.en: Teachers must report any incident involving a fight.
examples.cn: 任何涉及打斗的事件，教师都必须上报。

examples.en: The broken window was a small incident in an otherwise quiet term.
examples.cn: 这扇窗户被打破，只算是本该平静的一学期中的小插曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 在上 + cid 落 + -ent 名词词尾——落到你头上的一件事，就是事件

root: 拉丁语 incidere「落在上面」（in「在上」+ cadere「落下」）的分词 incidens 作名词，经法语 incident 于十五世纪进入英语；先泛指发生之事，后经警务与军事通报固定为「事故、冲突事件」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an event worth reporting, a small episode in a larger story, and an accident or clash in official language.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：值得上报的事件，长故事里的小插曲，以及官方用语中的事故与冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spilled milk bottle and a ring of glass under a street lamp in the morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨路灯下，一只打翻的牛奶瓶和一圈碎玻璃。

branches.en: THE EVENT: incident names a happening that draws notice.
branches.cn: 事件线：incident 指一件引人注意的事。

branches.en: THE EPISODE: inside a story it marks one small chapter.
branches.cn: 插曲线：放在故事里，它标明一个很小的章节。

branches.en: THE REPORT: police and army language fixed it on accidents and clashes.
branches.cn: 通报线：警务与军事语言把它固定在事故与冲突上。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: without incident means all went as planned.
branches.cn: 搭配线：without incident 表示一切如常。

branches.en: THE PAIR: incidence measures how many times such events occur.
branches.cn: 对照线：incidence 量的是这类事件出现的次数。

intro.en: The table gathers words built on the Latin root cadere, to fall.
intro.cn: 此表汇集以拉丁词根 cadere「落下」为底的词。

latinIntro.en: Cadere with different prefixes produces accident, incident, occasion and decay.
latinIntro.cn: cadere 配上不同前缀，就有了 accident、incident、occasion 与 decay。

items.example: One small incident changed the mood.
items.exampleCN: 一件小事改变了气氛。

items.example: Baggage fees are incidental costs.
items.exampleCN: 行李费属于附带费用。

items.example: Incidentally, the shop closes early today.
items.exampleCN: 顺便说一下，今天店关得早。

items.example: The incidence of the disease has doubled.
items.exampleCN: 这种病的发生率翻了一倍。
